title: Associate Manager - IOS Flutter
description:
IMEA (India, Middle East, Africa) India LIXIL INDIA PVT LTD Employee Assignment Hybrid Full Time 31 October 2026

Senior Mobile Engineer (iOS & Flutter)

As a Senior Mobile Engineer on our international team, you will play a key role in creating fast, reliable mobile apps that connect with our smart IoT (Internet of Things) systems. We are looking for a flexible developer who is skilled in both native iOS and Flutter, and ready to switch between the two platforms as project needs evolve. You will write clean code, champion modern programming practices, and take ownership of our apps—whether you are building a brand new concept from scratch or improving and scaling applications that are already live in production.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and deploy advanced, scalable applications for iOS and cross-platform environments.
  • Architect maintainable codebases utilizing modern design patterns such as MVVM, Clean Architecture, and Modularization.
  • Bridge native iOS modules with Flutter applications seamlessly using Platform Channels.
  • Lead technical execution and collaborate within an Agile ecosystem to define, design, and ship new features.
  • Manage the complete mobile application lifecycle, including provisioning, CI/CD pipeline integration, and App Store Connect distribution.
  • Refactor and integrate legacy Objective-C code with modern Swift and SwiftUI architectures.
  • Identify bottlenecks, troubleshoot bugs, and optimize overall application performance and UI/UX fidelity.
  • Document technical decisions and architecture clearly to align cross-functional teams and stakeholders.

Requirements

  • Experience: 5+ years of professional software development experience in mobile engineering.
  • Native iOS: Mastery of Swift and SwiftUI; deep functional experience with UIKit, and a strong working knowledge of Objective-C for legacy integration.
  • Hybrid Development: Highly proficient in Flutter and Dart, with proven experience bridging Flutter and Native modules.
  • Architecture & Design: Demonstrated ability to implement and scale modern design patterns (MVVM, Clean Architecture).
  • Tooling: Power user of Xcode (including Instruments and Debugging) alongside Android Studio or VS Code.
  • Version Control: Advanced Git capabilities, including branching strategies, rebasing, and complex conflict resolution.
  • Workflow: Strong familiarity with task management and technical documentation using Jira and Confluence.
  • Deployment: Hands-on experience with mobile CI/CD pipelines and App Store distribution.
  • Communication: High-level English proficiency with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts to both developers and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Product Mindset: A strong product-first approach with a critical eye for UI/UX detail, user-centric problem solving, and overall app performance.

title: Lead Data Analyst
description:
What You Will Do:
  • Lead the design, enhancement, and support of Power BI reports, dashboards, semantic models, and reporting solutions to deliver reliable business insights.
  • Investigate data quality issues, reporting discrepancies, and business logic gaps by performing root-cause analysis and partnering with data engineering teams to drive resolution.
  • Develop and optimize SQL queries, Power BI datasets, DAX measures, Power Query transformations, and reporting performance to improve scalability and user experience.
  • Build and maintain data pipelines and analytical solutions using Azure Data Factory (ADF) and Databricks, ensuring trusted and accessible data for reporting and analytics.
  • Collaborate with supply chain stakeholders to understand business processes, gather requirements, and translate business challenges into scalable analytics solutions.
  • Drive data standardization through reusable datasets, certified semantic models, governed KPIs, and consistent business definitions that enable self-service analytics.
  • Identify, prototype, and implement AI-enabled analytics solutions, including conversational analytics, chatbot experiences, and natural language querying using tools such as Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Azure AI, and Databricks AI/BI Genie.
  • Validate data transformations, business rules, and analytical models to ensure accuracy, governance, security, and alignment with business objectives.
  • Enable data democratization by empowering business users to independently access, explore, and analyze trusted enterprise data with minimal reliance on centralized reporting teams.
  • Own analytics initiatives end-to-end, from problem definition and solution design through validation, deployment, adoption, and continuous improvement, while driving stakeholder engagement and data-driven decision making.

What You will Need:
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Supply Chain, or a related discipline.
  • 7+ years of relevant experience in business analysis, Data analytics, business intelligence, or supply-chain analytics, with demonstrated hands-on solution delivery.
  • Strong SQL skills, with the ability to independently investigate complex datasets, reconcile discrepancies, and perform root-cause analysis.
  • Strong Power BI expertise, including data modeling, DAX, Power Query, semantic models, report optimization, and troubleshooting.
  • Secondary technical skillset – Databricks, Data Governance, Data Science Models, App Development
  • Strong ADF expertise on building pipelines, running transformations and fabricating the end-end flow with best practices.
  • Practical Python skills for data analysis, validation, or prototyping.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop prototypes, solve problems independently, and collaborate effectively with business and engineering teams.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

title: Assistant Project Manager Intern (Building Automation) - Summer 2027
description:
Overview

Interested in kickstarting your career in Project Management in the Construction Industry? Join Egan's Building Automation team this summer as an Assistant Project Manager Intern! From schools and hospitals to high-rise buildings and manufacturing facilities, our team helps bring buildings to life through innovative technology that makes them smarter, more efficient, and comfortable for the people who use them. As an intern, you'll gain hands-on experience supporting the coordination of projects that integrate heating and cooling systems, lighting controls, energy management, and intelligent building technologies.

In our summer internship program, you'll work alongside professionals in the industry while also engaging in events just for interns, including a jobsite ride along, Insights Discovery Workshop, mentorship opportunities, and more! Our internship program lasts 12 weeks, with flexible start and end dates to meet the needs of your school and extracurricular schedule.

If you're excited to learn, thrive in a fast-moving setting, and contribute to the success of impactful projects, we'd be thrilled to have you join our team this summer!

Responsibilities

The responsibilities of the Assistant Project Manager Intern include but are not limited to the following:

  • Collaborate with project team to plan, setup, and manage construction projects.
  • Navigate and use Egan’s project management systems and processes, including Milestone Based Delivery (MBD).
  • Become familiar with the materials, equipment, and components of the technical systems installed by Egan’s trades.
  • Assist senior staff by observing, learning, and doing the following:
    • Manage projects from start to finish
    • Set up project to meet or exceed budgetary and timing goals.
    • Order equipment and materials.
    • Attend job site meetings.
    • Manage people in various trades on the job sites.
    • Estimate jobs
    • Close out job with maximum profitability and customer satisfaction.
    • Advise project management of potential problems, work interferences, schedule difficulties, and the like, as it relates to assigned duties. Learn how Egan can circumvent and/or resolve such problems.
    • Track job permitting.
    • Develop and foster long-term relationships with customers through quality performance of work.
  • Promote a positive safety culture by following Egan’s safety policies.
  • Participate in construction document analysis to develop clear and consistent interpretations.
  • Compose and edit letters, memos, reports, and procedures; assist with change orders, project billings, and change request pricing.
  • Process day-to-day administrative items (i.e. supply requisitions, RFI’s, submittals, shop drawings, procurement, take-offs, etc.) as directed.
  • Build strong internal partnerships; work collaboratively with other Egan groups to support Egan’s Mission, Vision and Values.
  • Use basic understanding of financials and reporting to support a PM in related responsibilities.
  • Actively participate in Egan’s Summer Internship Program and activities.
  • Perform additional duties and assignments as requested/needed.

Requirements

  • Currently pursuing a two or four year degree in Construction Management, Mechanical or Electrical Construction, Engineering, Design, or related field.
  • 0-2 years of construction and/or general business experience.
  • Travel to jobsites and client sites may be required.

Qualifications

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Passion for the industry.
  • Outstanding organizational skills; ability to handle multiple priorities.
  • Courteous, professional, diplomatic, and highly motivated.
  • Anticipates and adjusts to changing priorities and methods; willingly takes on new tasks and challenges.
  • Excellent MS Office and Google Suite skills and ability/desire to learn new software systems.

Working Conditions

  • Performance of duties will mostly be in the Champlin office with visits to job sites as needed.
  • Ability to stand or sit for extended periods of time.
  • Exposure to loud noise, dirt, and exposure to the elements.
  • Climbing ladders/stairs, uneven ground, bending, kneeling, and twisting are frequent needs.

Benefits, Perks and Pay Beyond the Industry Standard

Egan is committed to providing a workplace that helps you thrive both personally and professionally.

  • Well-being: you’re offered comprehensive mental healthcare and support for you and your family
  • Professional Development: we support your learning and career growth by offering regular learning and development opportunities both on the job and as part of the summer internship program.
  • Community Involvement: our “Beyond the Jobsite” program supports causes in the communities in which we live and work through regular volunteer events to connect with each other and help those in need
  • Earned Sick and Safe Time (ESST): accrue paid leave that can be used for certain reasons related to sickness and safety

This internship provides a valuable learning experience and the opportunity to gain practical skills and experience. Please note that this is a temporary position and does not include company-sponsored benefits, like health insurance.

Pay Rate: $23.00 per hour

Strong Culture Built on Values and Keeping Promises

At Egan, you’ll be part of a team that shares a passion for redefining the industry by setting a new standard of customer care. Together, we'll promote teamwork, embrace innovation, act with integrity, pursue growth, and prioritize safety. You’ll have the opportunity to grow and develop in a company committed to providing the growth and success you're looking for, both for yourself and for the customers you serve. You’ll love being part of success shaped by the strength of our team, which is enhanced by:

  • Solid history as a legacy leader in specialty contracting and system integration for over 80 years
  • Private ownership and operations by employees who work in the company (not a holding company or private equity firm)
  • Engaging leadership who prioritizes your safety, your development, and your impact
  • A proven track record of employee retention and loyalty

From general contractors and architects to building owners and facility engineers, Egan collaborates throughout the entire construction or project process with the shared goal of maintaining best-in-class relationships with our internal teams, customers, and business partners. At over 1,000 employees occupying our offices and work sites, we aim to ensure every project is done with quality craftsmanship, integrity, and an aggressive commitment to safety. In fact, we’re proud to be recognized as one of America's Safest Companies for recurring years.

Application Instructions and Employment Practices

Egan Company will not discriminate against or harass any employee or application for employment because of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation), disability, age, genetic information (including family medical history), veteran status, marital status, familial status, local human rights commission activity, or status with regard to public assistance.

We do not accept application materials by mail or email except as a reasonable accommodation for qualified disabled applicants. Individuals who are unable to use our online process due to a disability should email recruiting@eganco.com.

Creating and maintaining a safe and drug-free working environment is important to all of us. Employment with Egan requires successful completion of a pre-employment drug screening. We also participate in E-Verify.

title: Performance & Cost Improvement Senior Manager
description:
Performance & Cost Improvement Senior Manager - Life Sciences & Health Care

Our Deloitte Strategy & Transactions team helps guide clients through their most critical moments and transformational initiatives. We offer comprehensive end-to-end support and advisory services, covering areas such as valuation modeling, cost optimization, restructuring, business design and transformation, infrastructure and real estate, mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and sustainability. The team works closely with clients at every stage of their journey, helping them navigate challenges, avoid financial pitfalls, and implement practical solutions before, during, and after major transformational projects or transactions creating lasting impact.

Deloitte's Performance & Cost Improvement (P&CI) team, part of Performance Improvement & Restructuring (PI&R), is seeking a Senior Manager to help organizations improve profitability, cash flow, and operating performance during complex transformations. Join the team dedicated to working with Life Sciences and Health Care (LSHC) clients to lead high-impact work across cost transformation, operating-model redesign, and M&A-related value creation for biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and medical device organizations.

Work You'll Do

As an LSHC Senior Manager on the Performance & Cost Improvement team, you will be responsible for leading client engagements that improve profitability, cash flow, and operating performance.
  • Lead cost transformation, productivity improvement, operating-model change, and M&A integration or separation workstreams for Life Sciences and Health Care clients.
  • Conduct client interviews and analyze financial and operational data from multiple sources to identify value-creation, cost-reduction, and performance-improvement opportunities.
  • Develop and present client-ready analyses, models, and implementation recommendations for senior client stakeholders.
  • Lead workstream planning and execution; oversee junior staff, review work products, and maintain quality control of client deliverables.
  • Build client relationships; support proposal development, market-building activities, and the development of internal tools and templates.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to mentor and provide clear guidance to others

The Team
PI&R defines and leads enterprise Board and C-Suite agendas for non-distressed, underperforming, and distressed clients to improve margins, operational and financial performance, navigate financial difficulties, and improve cashflow to fund critical transformations.

title: Project Manager–Surveying, Site Planning & Permitting (Oil&Gas) in , United States
description:
Summary
The Project Manager (PM) leads assigned DJ Basin oil and gas projects in Colorado from scope development through site planning, civil design, permitting, delivery, and closeout. Reporting to the Portfolio Manager, the PM serves as the primary client contact and coordinates Surveying, Remote Sensing, GIS, Drafting, Civil Engineering, and Permitting. The role translates client objectives into defined deliverables, project phases, tasks, budgets, and timelines, then manages the dependencies and critical path connecting each department’s work.

Working with department leaders, the PM coordinates the collection of field and client information, creation of deliverables, and handoffs needed to move projects forward. The PM tracks progress and remaining effort, manages changes, and brings the right people together to resolve missing information, delays, or competing priorities. Success requires enough understanding of the services and workflows to ask informed questions and recognize how an issue in one phase affects the rest of the project. Professional land surveyors, professional engineers, and other discipline leads own technical execution, quality review, and technical approvals within their areas of responsibility. The PM coordinates these efforts to meet overall scope, schedule, budget, and quality commitments.

Expected Results In The Role

Assigned projects meet scope, schedule, budget, and quality commitments, with risks identified early and recovery actions coordinated with the appropriate leaders.

Field information, site plans, maps, exhibits, and permitting work progress through clear departmental handoffs, with dependencies and decisions managed to support the critical path.

Clients receive clear updates, realistic commitments, and dependable follow-through, with technical questions resolved by the appropriate specialists.

Hours, remaining effort, forecasts, and invoices reflect actual project progress; unexplained variances and scope changes receive timely review and action.

Proposals and changes reflect realistic effort and delivery assumptions, with required approvals and technical reviews completed before commitments or delivery.

Delays and scope changes are addressed through coordinated solutions, timely decisions, and updated plans that keep teams and clients aligned.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities
Scope, Schedule, and Client Coordination

Develop scopes, deliverables, assumptions, exclusions, and budgets with technical leads; confirm client and contract requirements and obtain proposal and pricing approvals.

Break projects into phases and tasks with clear owners, effort estimates, milestones, dependencies, and a critical path; align timelines with department capacity.

Serve as the primary client contact, lead status discussions, secure decisions, and communicate progress, risks, and revised commitments.

Survey, Mapping, and Field Coordination

Coordinate survey and remote sensing work through department leaders, aligning collection needs, field access, resources, and delivery dates with project dependencies.

Track the creation and transfer of survey data, maps, exhibits, and revisions between Survey, GIS, Drafting, and downstream teams.

Confirm receiving teams have the information needed to proceed; coordinate follow-up on missing inputs or concerns raised by technical reviewers.

Civil Site Planning and Permitting Coordination

Obtain client information, layout preferences, design criteria, and decisions for technical teams developing site plans, access, utilities, grading, and drainage.

Track decisions and revisions affecting multiple departments, confirming that teams receive current direction and incorporate changes into their work.

Integrate engineering deliverables and ECMC, local, and applicable federal permitting milestones and review cycles into the schedule with Civil Engineering and Permitting.

Project Controls, Change, and Problem Solving

Review weekly hours, costs, progress, and remaining effort with technical leads; investigate variances and update budgets and forecasts.

Complete time and expense reviews, resolve coding questions, and approve invoices within delegated authority; obtain required approvals for commercial exceptions.

Assess scope changes with affected departments, document impacts, and secure required approvals before revising budgets, schedules, or client commitments.

Identify delays and risks to the critical path; work with teams to develop alternatives, adjust sequencing or resources, and escalated decisions with recommendations.

Quality, Project Records, and General Duties

Coordinate required technical reviews and track comment resolution before delivery; discipline leads retain responsibility for technical quality and approval.

Maintain project records, complete closeout and final billing, and share lessons learned that improve planning and handoffs.

Follow company safety, quality, and data-security requirements; maintain accurate time records and perform other related duties as assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities
No direct supervisory responsibilities; provides technical guidance, mentoring, and support for the development of other team members.

Required Skills & Abilities

Project planning and scheduling: Define scope, break projects into phases and tasks, and maintain schedules that reflect dependencies, resource needs, and the critical path.

Service and workflow understanding: Working knowledge of survey/geospatial, civil/site, environmental, or permitting delivery sufficient to coordinate inputs, deliverables, and handoffs across related services.

Problem solving and change management: Recognize threats to project commitments, assess impacts with technical teams, and develop workable options with clear decisions and follow-through.

Client and team coordination: Clarify client requirements, manage concurrent assignments, secure decisions, and align commitments with department capacity and technical guidance.

Collaborative leadership and influence: Build trust and gain agreement across departments without direct supervisory authority. Understand competing priorities, involve others in developing solutions, and use tact when providing feedback, resolving disagreements, and addressing missed commitments while maintaining productive working relationships.

Financial and effort judgment: Interpret budgets, hours, progress, and remaining work; investigate variances with technical leads and apply scope and approval requirements.

Organization and teamwork: Maintain reliable project records, use Microsoft 365 and project tools effectively, and collaborate across departments while demonstrating Ascent’s core values.

Skills & Abilities

title: Technology Intern
description:
Tech Intern — GoGro

Shopify & web development · D2C · Early-stage startup

Location: Gurgaon (Sector 32) · Work from office

Type: 6-month paid internship with a monthly stipend

PPO: Pre-placement offer for a full-time role, based on performance

Start: Immediate

Reports to: Co-founder

The role in summary

Own the website end to end : build it, grow its traffic, and turn visitors into customers. This is not a role where you take tickets and wait. You will be the person who knows the site best. You will spot what's broken, find out what's next and ship it.

About GoGro

GoGro is an early-stage, D2C brand building a Stage-Right Development System for children aged 0–7: developmental toys, physical play kits and online tools, each designed for a specific stage, with expert-backed guidance for parents. Founded by experienced entrepreneur, the company operates at the intersection of neuroscience, early childhood development, and consumer products.

What you will own

Build and run the Shopify store

  • Build new pages, sections, landing pages and modules for kit launches, campaigns and partnerships
  • Customise the theme in Liquid, HTML, CSS and Java , beyond what the theme editor allows
  • Integrate Shopify apps and third-party APIs (reviews, sub ions, email, WhatsApp, payments)
  • Keep the store fast, stable and bug-free on every device; manage products, collections and offers
  • Get the store ready for international markets: multi-currency, shipping and localisation

Get found: SEO, AEO and AAO

  • SEO: technical and on-page SEO (schema, meta data, internal linking, Core Web Vitals) so we rank for what parents search
  • AEO (Answer Engine Optimisation): structure content so GoGro appears in Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity answers
  • AAO (AI Agent Optimisation): make our product data and checkout easy for AI shopping agents to read, compare and buy from

Own the conversion funnel

  • Own the numbers from first visit to purchase to repeat order
  • Run A/B tests on layouts, copy, offers and page flows, and act on the results
  • Set up analytics (GA4, Search Console, Meta Pixel, heatmaps) and share a monthly report with clear next steps

Build tools for parents

  • Build interactive widgets that help parents with their child's development
  • Help integrate the GoGro philosophy in our tech
Who you are

An owner, not an executor. You treat the site as your own product. You notice problems before anyone points them out, figure things out from docs and forums without hand-holding, and measure yourself by results, not tasks completed. This matters more to us than any other skill.

Must-have

  • Hands-on Shopify development: you have built or managed at least one live store (college, freelance and personal projects count)
  • Strong HTML, CSS and Java ; comfortable reading and editing Liquid
  • Basic Python and a working understanding of REST APIs: consuming third-party APIs, handling JSON, authentication and frontend-backend communication
  • A working grasp of SEO and conversion basics
  • A sharp eye for design detail, and clear written and spoken English

Good to have

  • React.js
  • SEO, AEO or GEO work with results you can show
  • A/B testing and behaviour analytics tools (VWO, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar or similar)
  • Canva or Figma for quick banners and edits
  • Interest in D2C brands, parenting or early childhood

Education: B.E. or B.Tech from a Tier 1 engineering college, final year or recent graduate. Your Shopify portfolio carries as much weight as your degree.

What you get

  • A monthly stipend for 6 months, and a PPO for a full-time role in the GoGro team, based on performance
  • Real ownership of a live D2C brand's website from day one, not a sandbox project
  • Early-stage startup experience: speed, breadth, and work that real parents see every day
  • Direct mentorship from seasoned Founders who built one of India's largest parenting platforms
  • Exposure to an international D2C launch
  • Internship certificate and letter of recommendation

What success looks like
  • 30 days: You know the store inside out, have fixed the obvious issues and set up funnel tracking.
  • 3 months: You ship new pages within days of a request, A/B tests run every month, and the first parent tool is live.
  • 6 months: Traffic, AI visibility and conversion are measurably up, two parent tools are live, and the store is ready for new kits and international markets.
How to apply
  1. Your CV
  2. Links to Shopify stores or websites you have built or managed, with a line on your role in each
  3. A short note (under 200 words): three things you would build on a D2C website to grow traffic or conversion, and one tool you would build for parents. Send to helloatgogrotoysdotcom

title: Nuclear Reactor Operator in , United States
description:
Nuclear Reactor Operator

As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation's largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we're creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country's energy needs today and tomorrow.
Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more.
Pay Rate: $68.09/hr
Primary Purpose Of Position

The qualified individual will be responsible for the following:
Obtaining and maintaining an NRC license for operation of the facility.
Assigned on a rotating shift basis, acting under prescribed rules and approved practices, to observe, inspect and as instructed operate station equipment; to prepare equipment for service and for maintenance; to test equipment for proper operation; to take necessary action in emergencies; and to perform related work as assigned.
Specifically tied to NRC regulations includes the control of reactivity systems that affect power levels of the plant.
Monitoring gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine/system are working properly. Controlling operations of equipment or systems remotely from main control room center. Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents, licenses Critical Thinking, using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.
Assisting Senior Reactor Operators for finding and evaluating Information to determine compliance with required standards
Using relevant information and individual judgment to determine whether events or processes comply with laws, regulations, or standards and provide information to required parties.
Gathering Information, observing, receiving, and otherwise obtaining information from all relevant sources. Identifying Objects, Actions, and Events; identifying information by categorizing, estimating, recognizing or similarities, and detecting changes in circumstances or events.
Monitoring Processes, Materials, or Surroundings
Monitoring and reviewing information from materials, events, or the environment, to detect or assess problems. Documenting/Recording Information
Entering, transcribing, recording, storing, or maintaining information in written or electronic form.
Primary Duties And Accountabilities

Observe, inspect, and as instructed, operate such generating station auxiliary equipment as pumps, fans, air compressors, and heat exchangers.
Inspect and make necessary adjustment on gland seal pressures on main turbine generator units.
Make routine checks of various equipment related to transfer of water and steam.
Inspect and reset relays in auxiliary power centers in the event of automatic trip-out of any auxiliary equipment.
Operate auxiliary equipment manually when remote control equipment is not connected to the main control panel, or during abnormal conditions.
Assist as required in performing initial troubleshooting work on control circuit, auxiliary switches, tripping devices on circuit breakers, and level controllers.
Perform manual switching in auxiliary power centers for all routine maintenance or emergency repairs to electrical equipment.
Check the operation of feed water heaters and other secondary plant equipment such as station heating, ventilating and cooling systems.
Inspect auxiliary power transformers, switchgear, and batteries by checking the temperature of equipment, oil levels in transformers, acid levels in batteries; and to record specific gravity readings and charge batteries as required.
Operate the water treatment system, involving such work as adjusting feed of chemical feed pumps, preparing chemicals for feed tanks and make-up pretreatment, checking levels in storage tanks, adjusting rates of flow, recording of chemicals used and water meter readings, and making field checks on water samples as assigned.
Operate oil cleaning and transfer equipment, including checking all levels in reservoirs, back flushing oil coolers, and periodically taking oil samples.
Inspect brushes on main generator field rings on various motor generator sets; and to check exciter bearings.
Replace gas cylinders (e.g. hydrogen, nitrogen) on headers; to check the operation of the hydrogen unit gas dryer.
Maintain cleanliness of equipment and working area.
Assist in controlling the operation of reactor-turbine generator units by receiving and executing orders from station operators, observing control instruments, and reading meters.
Observe, inspect and operate reactor, turbine and other station equipment outside of the control room (including starting, stopping and preparing equipment for maintenance).
Perform electrical operating and switching outside the control room, such as operating disconnects, circuit breakers, and grounding buses; and to take circuits and equipment in and out of service.
Instruct and train, and to coordinate the work of others.
Other assigned duties may include activities in the field outside the main control room:
Minimum Qualifications

Candidates must possess at least a High School Diploma or equivalent.
Candidates with a college degree will need to provide transcripts.
Candidates with applicable military experience (e.g., Navy Nuclear) will need to provide DD214 (long form) and training history.
Candidates must pass the Plant Operator Selection System (POSS) examination and Basic Math and Science Test (BMST) [administered by the Talent Acquisition Department].
Candidates must successfully complete a License Medical Screening and Fire Brigade Screening prior to introduction into the Non-Initial Licensed Operator Training Program.
Candidates must satisfactorily complete a psychological screening.
Candidates must qualify for site unescorted access.
Candidates must meet the power plant experience requirements of ACAD 10-001 or company governance.
Per ACAD 10-001 candidates must Meet or exceed one of the following:
6 months performing plant operational duties as a non-licensed operator on-site at the Constellation nuclear power plant for which you are applying as an RO (qualified for all power block and safety system operational duties). Must have 18 months total Power Plant experience OR
12 months experience performing plant operational duties as a qualified non-licensed operator at a comparable nuclear facility or 18 months at a noncomparable nuclear facility (qualified for all power block and safety system operational duties). Comparable is PWR to PWR or BWR to BWR, and non-comparable is PWR to BWR or BWR to PWR. Must have 18 months total Power Plant experience OR
6 months performing plant operational duties as an ACTIVE licensed reactor operator at a comparable nuclear facility or 12 months experience at a noncomparable commercial power reactor operator facility. Comparable is PWR to PWR or BWR to BWR, and non-comparable is PWR to BWR or BWR to PWR. Must have 18 months total Power Plant experience OR
18 months in position equivalent to the reactor operator position at a miliary Navy Reactor (qualified to manipulate or direct the manipulation of control rods. The equivalent positions are Reactor Operator, Engineering Officer of the Watch / Propulsion Plant Watch Officer, Engineering Watch Supervisor / Propulsion Plant Watch Supervisor OR
27 months of experience performed in a non-nuclear power production plant during preoperational, startup testing or operational activities. Other acceptable experience includes plant design, construction, technical support, operation, maintenance, or training instruction with respect to petrochemical; similar process plants; or steam propulsion plants.

  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor(s)

title: Quality & Validation Lead (Director Level)
description:
THE ROLE

Valkai builds AI agents for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies. As our Quality & Validation Lead, you’ll build the function that makes it possible for customers to qualify Valkai for regulated work. You’ll own our quality management system (QMS) and be the person our customers turn to when they need to know what changed in a release, how it was tested, and what it means for their validated workflows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll write and roll out core procedures, review validation evidence, and lead customer audits yourself.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Build and run Valkai’s QMS. Set the quality roadmap, choose the tools, and put standard operating procedures (SOPs), document control, training, deviation management, and corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) into practice. Define process owners, track quality metrics, and lead management reviews.

  • Put risk-based validation into the software release process. Work with Product and Engineering to document requirements, link them to test evidence, and establish change control. Define when a release needs additional testing, revalidation, or customer notification.

  • Help teams validate Valkai. Build a reusable package of validation plans, test evidence, traceability, and release impact assessments. Work with AI Strategy and customer quality teams to define what Valkai will test and document and what the customer will validate for its intended use.

  • Lead quality audits and customer diligence. Host customer audits, respond to quality questionnaires, and run a risk-based internal audit and supplier qualification program. Own corrective actions through verified closure and support customer inspections when Valkai evidence is needed.

  • Shape the product roadmap for regulated use. Use findings from customer deployments, validation reviews, and audits to identify which gaps prevent customers from going live. Work with Product and Engineering to turn recurring needs into product requirements and prioritize capabilities such as audit trails, configurable approvals, and workflow version history.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Experience building or substantially scaling a QMS at a life sciences software vendor or within a regulated life sciences organization. You’ve personally written SOPs and put quality processes into use.

  • Hands-on experience with risk-based computerized system validation (CSV) for cloud software, including reviewing validation plans, traceability, test evidence, and release changes.

  • Working knowledge of GxP, data integrity, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, and EU GMP Annex 11, with judgment about when those requirements apply.

  • Experience leading audits and closing findings. You can defend a risk decision with a quality leader and turn it into work an engineering team can implement.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience qualifying a GxP SaaS vendor or supporting regulated software deployments across multiple life sciences customers.

  • Experience validating AI-enabled workflows or putting model, prompt, and configuration changes under change control.

  • Experience as an early quality hire or selecting and rolling out an electronic QMS.

BENEFITS

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents.

  • Generous paid time off and paid parental leave.

At Valkai, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran status.

title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer

You are energized by ambiguity, motivated by customer outcomes, and able to influence organizational change alongside the technical work.

**What you'll do here**

- Capture structured product feedback from customer deployments and advocate directly with engineering and product teams for roadmap and usability improvements.


**What we're looking for**

- 5+ years of experience in a Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Architect, Platform Engineering, or equivalent post-sales technical role, with a demonstrated track record of guiding enterprise customers through complex technical deployments.

- Proven hands-on experience from a prior role designing and deploying cloud infrastructure on at least one major provider: AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure; you have done the work and can speak to it with specificity.

- 2+ years of production experience with Kubernetes: cluster design, workload scheduling, networking, storage, and operational lifecycle.

- 2+ years of experience with Terraform or equivalent infrastructure-as-code tooling; you understand how enterprise teams structure, version, and maintain IaC at scale.

- Solid understanding of Linux systems administration, including networking fundamentals: ingress controllers, proxies, load balancers, and DNS resolution in cloud-native environments.

- Familiarity with CI/CD pipeline design and DevOps practices; you understand how code moves from commit to running workload in an enterprise context.

- Working knowledge of cloud security and identity: IAM patterns, network segmentation, secrets management, and compliance-relevant controls.

- Understanding of observability practices including logging, metrics, and tracing across distributed systems

- Experience with AI tooling at both the user level (coding agents, assistants) and infrastructure level (model proxies, LLM routing layers such as LiteLLM).

- Demonstrated ability to design repeatable delivery patterns, not just solve one-off problems.

- Comfort working through organizational and workflow change alongside technical change with customers.

- Strong verbal and written communication skills: you can hold a room with a senior infrastructure team and produce a clear architecture document without those being separate skills.

- High customer empathy: you understand that the best technical solution does not always fit a customer's constraints, timeline, or organizational reality.

- Self-directed, analytically minded, and comfortable operating with full autonomy in a startup environment.


**Bonus tacos if you have**

- (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

- Experience at both early-stage startups and larger software organizations.

- Background as a Software Engineer, DevOps Engineer, or Platform Engineer before moving into a customer-facing role.

- Familiarity with regulated environments: air-gapped deployments, network isolation, SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, or DORA requirements.

- Experience with disaster recovery design and multi-region availability patterns.

- Cloud cost optimization experience, including rightsizing, reserved capacity, and FinOps practices.

- Experience with Tailscale or similar overlay networking tools.

- Kubernetes certification (CKA, CKAD, or CKS).

- Open-source contributions.

- Experience with Backstage.io or similar internal developer portals and platform tooling.

- Prior work on or alongside a developer platform or platform engineering team.

- Experience introducing new operating models or delivery patterns across post-sales or go-to-market teams.


### **About Coder**

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. **Permitted**: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.

- **Ashby** and **Brainerr** help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

- **Granola** takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.


All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. In accordance with New York City Local Law 144, an independent bias audit has been conducted on "Automated Employment Decision Tools"; results are available for [Ashby](https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf).

If you're applying for a role at Coder and have questions about how we use AI in our process, or if you'd like to request information about the data we collect, please contact [careers@coder.com](mailto:careers@coder.com).

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description:
**Grade UE07: £41,885 - £49,798 per annum**

**College of Science and Engineering / School of GeoSciences / Global Change research Institute**

**Full-time: 35 hours per week**

**Fixed-term: for 36 months**

**Help us redefine what’s possible. Be part of something bigger.**

The University of Edinburgh isn’t just any employer. We are part of a local community and a contributor to global thinking, progress and research. Our people have helped shape the modern world and continue to work on research and ideas that make a difference to society.

Here, you can make a meaningful impact, take on new challenges and develop your career. Be part of something bigger, where your work has real impact and your development matters.

**About the role**

We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA) to join Antarctic Futures, an exciting new research project based at the School of GeoSciences, University of Edinburgh.

Antarctica is one of the most rapidly changing environments on Earth, yet we still lack a reliable understanding of how its terrestrial ecosystems function and respond to environmental change. Antarctic Futures aims to address this knowledge gap by developing the first biologically validated estimates of terrestrial ecosystem productivity and phenology across Antarctica.

Working within an international, multidisciplinary research team, you will play a central role in delivering this ambitious project. Your main focus will be integrating physiological field measurements with remote sensing data to quantify vegetation productivity and seasonal activity across Antarctic landscapes.

The role will involve preparing for and participating in an extended field campaign on Signy Island, Antarctica, during the 2027/28 austral summer (November 2027–March 2028). You will subsequently lead substantial elements of the data processing, analysis and modelling, integrating physiological, environmental and spectral datasets to develop landscape-scale estimates of ecosystem productivity.

This is an excellent opportunity to gain experience in Antarctic field research, plant physiological ecology, remote sensing and interdisciplinary environmental science. You will work closely with researchers across the UK and international partner institutions, contribute to scientific publications and help develop new approaches to monitoring and conserving Antarctic terrestrial ecosystems.

We are looking for someone with a background in ecological or environmental research, strong quantitative and analytical skills, and an enthusiasm for collaborative, interdisciplinary science.

**Why join us?**

- Professional development and subject matter expertise
- Opportunities to develop new skills and broaden your experience
- Leading-edge research
- Opportunities for publication

**Hours and working arrangements**

This is a full-time post (35 hours per week). We are open to considering flexible working arrangements and requests for hybrid working, where the role allows, on a non-contractual basis.

We would love to hear from you. Apply to join us and contribute to research that will transform our understanding of Antarctica’s terrestrial ecosystems.

title: Senior / Principal Environmental Consultant in , United States
description:
POSITION: Senior/Principal Environmental Consultant
LOCATION: New Jersey or Northeast United States

POSITION SUMMARY

AEI is seeking a Senior/Principal level environmental consultant to be a part of AEI’s expanding Site Mitigation team. The candidate will be a primary technical leader in the northeast region with an extension into other regions nationally as opportunities arise. The candidate will work alongside other senior level technical team members to oversee the implementation of a wide array of subsurface and remedial investigations, remedial action/mitigation projects, regulatory agency negotiations, and client or legal counsel communications. The candidate will support the leadership operations for the northeast region and nationally to assist in staff oversight, maintaining project technical quality and profitability objectives, and participating in operations and technical initiatives at the region and Division level. In addition, the candidate may work directly with the Division Lead and other senior level colleagues, to initiate and implement business development, client management, and technical service expansion activities in the northeast region and nationally. This is an opportunity for an individual to join a well-established company and technical team, while also playing a significant role in the continued development of the Site Mitigation Division.

LOCATION

Freehold or Cranford, NJ AEI offices are ideal, with other remote northeast US locations considered.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Experienced Principal level environmental consultant will assist with responding to incoming proposal requests and provide technical guidance to AEI’s sales team and their clients.
Perform technical reviews of prior environmental reports and develop / guide the development of proposals for appropriate next steps.
Serve as a subject matter expert for environmental regulatory programs in one or multiple states including New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Maryland and other states.
Provide technical leadership and strategic guidance on projects involving in the regulatory agencies.
Provide mentorship to junior staff and collaborate with peers regarding technical and regulatory matters as a subject matter expert.
Ability to understand and track project scopes, schedules, and budgets, and anticipate potential modifications and need for change orders
Will be responsible for overseeing and potentially managing the implementation of projects ranging from initial Phase II investigations to complex investigation and remediation projects involving regulatory oversight.
Provide senior level proposal and report reviews and perform writing of similar deliverables.
Ability to interpret data and has a strategic understanding of the required next steps.
Preparation of remedial cost estimates and environmental peer reviews.
Has strong industry relationships and maintains a favorable reputation among peers.
Maintains a current and thorough understanding of local and federal environmental regulations.
Will serve as a point of contact with regulatory agencies, clients, and their legal counsel, representing AEI and the Site Mitigation Division.
Develop cost effective and technically sound path-to-closures for a wide array of projects and environmental issues.
Participate in the operational management of the Site Mitigation east region with the Regional VP, and sometimes in the Division on a level.
May work with the Division lead to developing and implementing a Site Mitigation expansion plan for the northeast region, with potential contribution to other regions.
Depending on experience and interest, may initiate and participate in business development activities and foster relationship development on behalf of AEI and the Site Mitigation Division. Activities may include conference attendance, preparation of technical papers/blogs/presentations, and virtual or in person at client meetings.
Work collaboratively with other Senior/Principal team members and support training and oversight of junior staff.
Upholds a strong work ethic and demonstrates high quality technical consulting work.

QUALIFICATIONS

15+ years of experience as an environmental consultant performing technical work and successful project management.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; strong business acumen.
An entrepreneurial spirit with enthusiasm for being a primary contributor to growth. self-starter, resourceful, with attention to detail and the ability to work productively.
Senior level understanding of environmental contamination with transaction related project management a plus.
Understanding of project budgeting with operational finances a plus

EDUCATION

Bachelor’s Degree, or higher, in science related field

LICENSES / CERTIFICATIONS

Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG), and/or Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP) or similar are appreciated
Current OSHA 40-hour \"HAZWOPER\" training certification strongly , additional Health and Safety training a plus

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The work environment will consist of primarily remote desk office work, with occasional travel to AEI offices, industry events, occasional field visits to project sites, and/or client meetings may be required. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Outdoor work requires the ability to effectively perform work in all types of weather conditions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, type, handle office, and/or field equipment, speak and hear. The employee may occasionally be required to stand, walk, balance, kneel, or crouch. The employee may be required to travel independently and lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to focus.

EMPLOYEE BENEFITS & PERKS

AEI Consultants offers all full-time employees an outstanding, extensive benefits package, which among other benefits includes medical, dental, and vision benefits, paid time off and sick leave, life insurance, short-term and long-term insurance, 401K, complimentary use of AEI’s condo at Donner Lake in Truckee, CA, an Employee Referral Bonus Program, and Commuter Tax and Dependent Care Benefits.

COMPENSATION

This position offers a competitive base salary commensurate with qualifications and experience plus commission / incentives.

COMPANY CULTURE

One of the primary reasons that our employees enjoy working at AEI is our positive company culture. We offer a collaborative, flexible, and inclusive work environment where employees can engage in meaningful work, make a positive impact on our clients and communities, and are encouraged to carve out a career path within the organization that best aligns with their interests and goals. We value the contributions of our team members and prioritize employee wellness, safety, flexibility, and work/life balance.

OVERVIEW

AEI Consultants is an employee-owned consulting firm that provides comprehensive services to commercial lenders, property owners, managers, tenants, and developers, industries, institutions, government agencies, and insurers, including many Fortune 500 companies. These services include environmental, property and facility assessments, zoning and energy consulting, site investigation and remediation, industrial hygiene, land surveying, valuation, and construction risk management. AEI specializes in identifying potential risks and crafting solutions through Environmental and Building Evaluation Consulting, Construction Services, Site Investigation and Remediation expertise. AEI Consultants is known for being reliable, responsive, and resourceful. Founded in 1992, AEI is based in the San Francisco Bay area and has offices strategically located throughout the United States.

AEI Consultants values and is committed to fostering an inclusive environment for our employees and community. We encourage all applicants who are excited about this opportunity and share our career goals to apply, even if they do not meet every requirement. We are proud to offer equal employment opportunities, prohibiting discrimination and harassment based on various protected characteristics defined by law. This policy applies to all aspects of employment. At AEI Consultants, we believe that a diverse team is essential for our success, and we strive to attract, develop, and retain talented individuals from diverse backgrounds.

title: Nuclear Engineering & Safeguards Experts for Red Team in , United States
description:
About the work
Mercor is assembling a panel of nuclear domain experts to red-team frontier AI models. The goal is to test whether a model can correctly judge the misuse potential of a technical request — answering legitimate questions fully while refusing genuinely dangerous ones.

You will:

Write challenging single-turn prompts in your domain, labelled across three levels: benign, dual-use, and adversarial.

Evaluate the responses that come back against a defined policy standard, and judge whether each was handled correctly.

Write the reference answer; what a correct response looks like, and the technical reasoning for why.
Background we’re looking for
We’re looking for fuel-cycle depth plus some exposure to how material is controlled, accounted for, or diverted. Safeguards and nonproliferation experience is the strongest signal. The red-teaming task is to write prompts that pull a model past the boundary; the plausible research framing, the question that looks academic until you know what it’s actually asking for — and then to explain in writing why the response was or wasn’t acceptable.
Examples of relevant backgrounds (Ideally w/Red-teaming experience): Safeguards Analyst / IAEA or Euratom Inspector — material accountancy, inspection regimes, Additional Protocol. Nuclear Engineer, Fuel Cycle — enrichment, reprocessing and criticality, end to end. Nuclear Security Engineer ( laboratory) — MPC&A, insider threat, physical protection design. Nuclear Forensics Scientist — radioxenon monitoring, attribution, detection and characterisation. Nonproliferation Analyst — export control, NSG trigger lists, acquisition and smuggling pathways.
What the work requires
This is writing-intensive work. Every judgment you make needs a written rationale that a non-specialist can follow. Prior technical writing, published research, or expert witness experience is a strong signal — please include a sample or link. You will also be reading and writing about misuse scenarios in your field for sustained periods. We brief experts on this in advance, and you can pause or step away at any point without penalty.
Before you apply
Your work here will not involve, and must not draw on, classified or export-controlled information, or anything covered by an NDA or prepublication review obligation. If you hold such obligations you may still be a good fit — tell us in your application and we will scope the work accordingly.

They guide the technical direction of design solutions while collaborating with the Software, Controls, and Electronics teams to execute detailed development.

Success in this position comes from strong systems thinking, the ability to conceptualize and evaluate new technologies, and the leadership to coordinate cross functional teams toward robust, manufacturable solutions aligned with Cummins’ long term product strategy.

In this role, you will make an impact in the following ways:

Concept Design, Development & System Architecture:

title: High School Principal
description:
Title: Principal

Organization: The STEAD School

Reports To: STEAD Board of Directors

Position Type: Full-Time, Year Round

Typical Calendar Days: 260

Position summary

The STEAD School is hiring a principal to work side by side with our staff, lead a school through a turnaround, and build it into what it was meant to be. The principal is STEAD's primary leader and is responsible for the school's culture, teaching and learning, safety, operations, finances and results, and for designing a clear, predictable organizational structure in which everyone knows their role and who they report to.

This is a role for an organizational leader. The principal will see clearly what is not working, build the systems and structures to fix it, and hold themselves and others accountable for results. He/she will also build trust with students, guides, families, the board and the wider community. This person will be candid about the work ahead and show the way by doing it alongside our staff.

This job will be very hard. We are looking for someone who wants it anyway, because they believe in what STEAD can be for young people.

About STEAD

STEAD stands for science, technology, environment, agriculture and design. We are a small, public charter high school where students learn through projects, hands-on work and real-world experience. Our teachers are called guides. Our community describes STEAD as close-knit, caring, unique and creative.

STEAD is known for:

  • Project-based learning (PBL), Accelerator weeks, internships, trips and on-campus agriculture.
  • Strong, respectful relationships between guides and students.
  • Student voice and leadership, through ambassadors, student council and a real say in the life of the school.

STEAD is not meant to be a traditional high school, and our community does not want it to become one. It is also not meant to lack structure. Our families, staff and students want a school that is both distinctive and well run.

The turnaround opportunity

STEAD is a school in turnaround, and we want every candidate to understand both the challenges and the opportunity before they apply.

  • Finances and compliance. The school is under serious financial strain. It has important financial and compliance obligations to meet, including in special education, with its lenders and its authorizer.
  • Enrollment. Enrollment is a serious challenge, and a new high school opens nearby next year.
  • Leadership and staff turnover. STEAD has had three leaders in under three years, and many guides have left. Those who remain are committed but stretched.
  • Missing systems and slipping expectations. Clear systems have fallen away, and expectations have slipped. Staff and students need a more predictable, consistent and safe environment.
  • An unclear identity. People love STEAD, but they cannot collectively say what it is and who it is for.

An interim principal is working now to stabilize the school and will prepare a handoff plan for the new principal. The new principal will be expected to carry out that plan during the transition period and the first six months, and then build on it.

Leading this turnaround will be demanding work. STEAD also has real strengths to build on: a fiercely loyal community, committed guides, students who care about their school, and an educational model worth fighting for.

How the principal will lead

STEAD has learned what works here. Leaders who felt distant, or who seemed to rule over the school, did not succeed. Leaders who worked side by side with staff and students, collaborated closely and stayed close to daily life did. The principal will lead the second way:

  • Learn STEAD's culture and listen before making major changes.
  • Work alongside guides in classrooms and in the daily work, not from a distance.
  • Share plans early, invite input and explain decisions.
  • Hold high expectations for adults and students, and model them.
  • Delegate clearly and hold people accountable with care.
  • Fix what is broken while protecting what makes STEAD special.
  • Tell the truth, including hard news.

Key responsibilities

Organizational leadership and improvement

  • Carry out the interim principal's handoff plan during the transition period and the first six months.
  • Build an accurate picture of what is and is not working across culture, instruction, safety, operations and finances.
  • Turn that diagnosis into a clear, written improvement plan that builds on the handoff plan, and lead it with relentless follow-through.
  • Put in place clear, fair and consistent systems for behavior, safety, attendance, schedules, communication and daily operations.
  • Monitor whether systems are working, using data and feedback, and adjust.

School culture, safety and expectations

  • Restore high expectations for learning, conduct and professionalism for students and adults alike.
  • Make sure all adults apply schoolwide expectations consistently.
  • Address vaping, drug use, conflict and other safety concerns directly.
  • Build a safe, respectful student culture that uses restorative practices alongside clear consequences.
  • Protect and strengthen student voice and leadership.

Teaching and learning

  • Deepen project-based learning, Hive, Accelerator weeks, internships, agriculture and student leadership.
  • Make sure the learning model is rigorous and that families understand it.
  • Coach guides in project-based learning and support their professional growth.
  • Improve attendance, student engagement and academic performance.

Staff leadership and supervision

  • Design and lead a clear, predictable organizational structure, with defined roles and lines of supervision and accountability across the leadership team and staff.
  • Delegate well and follow through.
  • Supervise, develop, coach and evaluate staff, and address performance honestly and with care.
  • Reduce turnover by building a staff culture where guides feel supported, heard and part of the work.
  • Protect planning time and pay attention to workload.

Finance, operations and compliance

  • Work with the board and finance team to build and manage a sustainable budget.
  • Meet all financial and compliance obligations to lenders and our authorizer, including special education compliance.
  • Oversee school operations so the school runs smoothly day to day.
  • Support fundraising.

Identity, enrollment and community

  • Lead students, guides, families and the board toward a shared, specific answer to what STEAD is and who it is for.
  • Lead recruitment and retention in a competitive market, including a new high school opening nearby.
  • Tell STEAD's story clearly to prospective families, partners and the community.

Communication and trust

  • Keep a regular, honest rhythm of communication with families, staff, students and the board, in the principal's own voice.
  • Be visible at school, in classrooms and at community events.
  • Work with the Parent Action Crew and community partners.
  • Report regularly to the Board of Directors on school performance, finances and progress on the improvement plan.

Qualifications

Required

  • Classroom teaching experience, so the principal understands a guide's daily work firsthand.
  • At least three years of school leadership experience, such as principal, assistant principal, dean or director of a school program, including supervising staff and managing a budget.
  • A track record of leading a school through a turnaround or significant improvement: diagnosing problems and building systems that measurably improved culture, safety, instruction or operations.
  • Experience in a project-based, expeditionary, Montessori, alternative or charter school setting, or a clear, demonstrated commitment to student-centered, hands-on learning.
  • Experience supervising, coaching and evaluating staff, including holding people accountable for performance.
  • An active Colorado principal license.

Preferred

  • Master's Degree in Educational Administration or Educational Leadership
  • High school leadership experience.
  • Experience leading an assistant principal or administrative team.
  • Experience stabilizing a school after leadership turnover.
  • Experience growing enrollment in a competitive school market.
  • Knowledge of charter school finance, compliance and authorizer relationships.
  • Knowledge of special education and student support services, including compliance.
  • Experience with fundraising and financial turnaround.
  • Experience leading in diverse communities and building trust with families from different backgrounds.
  • Familiarity with Colorado charter schools.
  • Interest in agriculture, environmental education or the sciences.

Skills and qualities

We are looking for a principal who is both a builder and a believer: someone who builds the systems a struggling school needs, and who believes in project-based learning and in the young people STEAD serves. In particular, we are looking for someone who is:

  • Relentless and resilient. Keeps pushing for improvement on hard days and slow weeks, and stays steady under pressure.
  • Systematic. Uses data, observation and conversation to find root causes, then designs, launches and adjusts clear systems.
  • Candid. Says plainly what is true, what needs to change and why, and communicates bad news well.
  • Collaborative and humble. Leads as "a leader, not a boss," listens to the people closest to the work, and acts on what they hear.
  • A relationship builder. Earns trust across groups with different priorities: staff, students, families, board members and the authorizer.
  • Caring, with deep respect for adolescents. Treats students as capable young people, never talks down to them, and helps them learn from poor choices.
  • Confident in hard conversations. Can be assertive and compassionate at once when holding staff or students accountable.
  • Honest and consistent. Does what they say they will do.
  • Committed for the long term. Wants to put down roots and see the work through.

Credentials matter, but they are not enough. We will weigh what candidates have actually done, how they did it, and whether they stayed, more than titles or an impressive resume.

Expectations for the transition and first six months

By the end of the first six months, the Board expects that:

  • The principal has carried out the handoff plan from the interim principal, beginning in the transition period.
  • The principal has spent real time listening and learning, in classrooms and with students, guides, families and partners, and has used that time as a diagnosis.
  • A written improvement plan that builds on the handoff plan has been shared with the community. It is candid about the challenges and clear about priorities.
  • Financial and compliance commitments, including special education compliance, are on track.
  • The leadership team has clear roles and clear lines of supervision and accountability.
  • Schoolwide expectations for behavior, safety and attendance are in place and applied consistently by adults.
  • Families, staff and students get regular, honest updates and see the principal around campus.
  • A community process to define what STEAD is and who it is for is under way.

The Board of Directors will set specific measures and targets with the new principal.

Governance and board partnership

  • The board establishes strategic direction, approves budgets and policies, and evaluates the principal.
  • The principal is responsible for daily school operations, implementation, staff supervision, and organizational performance.
  • The principal provides regular, accurate and transparent reporting to the board.
  • The principal identifies significant risks and communicates them promptly.
  • The board provides clear expectations, appropriate support, and consistent accountability.
  • The board does not bypass the principal to manage individual employees or day-to-day operations.

Compensation and benefits

  • Competitive salary based on experience and qualifications. The salary range is $125,000-$150,000. The principal may also be eligible for a performance bonus based on progress toward performance metrics set by the Board of Directors. Bonuses are not automatic.
  • A comprehensive benefits package that includes:
  • 100% employer-paid health, dental, vision and life insurance for the employee
  • 12+ hours of vacation per month
  • 401(k) with a 100% match up to 5% of compensation

Application process

Qualified candidates should submit:

  1. A cover letter (two pages or fewer) explaining why they want to lead STEAD specifically, and how their leadership approach fits a school that needs both stability and a strong, student-centered culture.
  2. A written response (two pages or fewer) describing a time they led a school or organization through a turnaround or significant improvement. Candidates should describe what they found, how they diagnosed the root causes, the systems and structures they put in place, how they brought staff, students and families along, and the measurable results. They should also share what they would do differently.
  3. A résumé or CV highlighting relevant experience, including school leadership, turnaround or improvement work, and work in project-based or alternative settings.
  4. Contact information for three professional references, including at least one person who supervised them and one person they supervised or coached.

Candidates who advance will complete performance tasks, such as analyzing school data to diagnose problems and propose systems, and will meet with students, staff and families.

The position will be posted from November 20, 2026, through January 4, 2027. Screening will take place in January, and interviews will take place from late January through early February. The ideal and preferred start date is spring 2027, with a transition alongside the interim principal through mid-April 2027.

Candidates should reach out to aodell@mingaeducationgroup.org with any questions.

Equal opportunity

The STEAD School is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive community. Candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Mandatory Background Checks: In alignment with our commitment to student safety, all candidates are required to undergo a comprehensive background check, which includes reviewing criminal records and will require fingerprinting. Please be aware that certain findings in the background check may disqualify a candidate from employment in a school setting. These may include, but are not limited to:



  • Convictions for violent crimes, such as assault or domestic violence.

  • Convictions for offenses against children, including abuse or endangerment.

  • Drug-related offenses, particularly those involving the distribution or trafficking of controlled substances.

  • Certain felony convictions, depending on their nature and recency.

  • History of certain misdemeanors that may raise concerns about a candidate's suitability for working in an educational environment. Submission of this application signifies your consent to this process and understanding of these criteria.


Verification of Qualifications: For roles that demand specific qualifications or certifications (such as teaching credentials), you will be asked to provide verifiable proof. We also conduct reference checks to validate your professional history and qualifications


Adherence to Colorado Education Laws: Our recruitment process strictly follows the guidelines and regulations set forth by the Colorado Department of Education. We expect all applicants to be familiar with and adhere to these standards.

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector.
