title: Research Assistant in Philosophy, Religion and History of Science
description:
- Location: Leeds - Main Campus
- Salary: £33,951 to £39,906 p.a.
- Contract type: Fixed Term (for 12 months to complete a specific task or time limited work, including the need for specific expertise or additional resource for a project.)
- Closing date: 13 December 2026

**Are you an early career researcher looking for your first challenge? Do you have a background in digital humanities and/or the history of science and technology? Do you want to further your career in one of the UK’s leading research intensive Universities?**

We are recruiting a Research Assistant for the AHRC-funded project ‘A woman’s work is never...shown? Histories of the ‘representation’ of women’s technoscientific labour since 1945’, which is led by Project Lead Dr Emily Rees and Co-Lead Professor Graeme Gooday. The project aims to recover visual representations of women’s technoscientific labour in archive and collections to better understand the role of women in technoscience in the UK after 1945 until c. 2000. Working with project partners the Institution of Engineering and Technology, the Science Museum Group, the Women’s Engineering Society and the International Network of Women Engineers and Scientists, the project will produce a dataset of archival metadata, case studies and analytical tools, a toolkit for using the dataset, practitioner interviews and academic articles, alongside three project workshops.

As Research Assistant, you will be in charge of managing and completing the dataset and writing the case studies (with input from the rest of the team). With experience in digital humanities and novel digital methods, you will lead on using digital tools to work with the archival images and dataset. Additionally, you will support on organising the workshops, writing the toolkit and processing the practitioner interview data. There will also be opportunities to contribute as a co-author on academic presentations and publications. You will be offered the chance to take an active role in the research life and culture of the School of PRHS. It is not necessary to live in or near Leeds, but you should be prepared to travel to Leeds on a montly basis for in-person meetings with the project team. Due to funding restrictions, the post is only available on a fixed-term basis for 12 months 0.5FTE.

**What we offer in return**

- 26 days holiday plus approx.16 Bank Holidays/days that the University is closed by custom (including Christmas) – That’s 42 days a year!

And much more!

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description:
**UE07: £41,885 - £49,798**

**School of Biological Sciences – Institute of Infection and Immunology Research**

**Full Time - 35 hours**

**Fixed term - 36 months**

**The Opportunity:**

Where discovery never stops. Be part of something bigger.

We are seeking an enthusiastic Postdoctoral Research Associate to investigate how early mammalian embryos defend themselves against viruses without a type I interferon response.

During early development, embryos suppress type I interferon signalling—the body’s most efficient antiviral defence. Suppressing this pathway may leave embryos vulnerable to viral infection.

This project will explore alternative antiviral mechanisms in embryonic cells, with a particular focus on RNA-binding proteins. These proteins may detect viral components and restrict infection, potentially including through RNA degradation. We aim to identify additional RNA-binding proteins that protect embryonic cells from viruses.

This project will combine approaches from virology, RNA biology, molecular biology, and functional genomics. Expertise in mammalian cell culture, viral infection assays, CRISPR-based perturbation, RNA-seq, proteomics, quantitative imaging, and computational analysis is highly valuable.

The applicant should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in virology, molecular biology, RNA biology, immunology, cell biology, genomics, or a related field. Experience in mammalian cell culture, molecular cloning, RNA analysis, viral infection assays, or bioinformatic analysis of sequencing data would be advantageous.

title: Postdoctoral Position in Solar Physics (m/w/d) in , United States
description:
The Institute for Solar Physics (KIS, Freiburg, Germany) invites applications for a two-year

postdoctoral position (m/w/d)

on the development of fast spectro-polarimetric (Stokes) inversion techniques.

The goal of the project is to optimize existing Stokes inversion codes using graphical processing units (GPUs) and machine-learning (ML) algorithms, substantially increasing the speed at which spectropolarimetric data can be analyzed and enabling near-real-time processing and interpretation. The project is based on preliminary work at KIS that shows the feasibility of this approach. The final goal is to extend the resulting code to a range of instruments, prioritizing those at GREGOR and the VTF at DKIST.

Qualifications: Applicants should hold a PhD in physics, astrophysics, applied mathematics, or a related field. Experience with radiative transfer and/or Stokes inversion techniques is highly desirable, and prior work with spectropolarimetric observations is an advantage. Familiarity with GPU programming (e.g., CUDA) and machine-learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) is also considered a plus.

The offer: The contract is for a period of 2 years. Salary and benefits are according to the rules for public employees of the State of Baden-Württemberg (TV-L) and German law, at the TV-L E-13 level. On top of the regular social security plans, it includes contributions to a supplementary pension plan, statutory health insurance, and a Christmas bonus.

The position could start as early as Jan.

1st, 2027 .

Deadline for applications: October 31st, 2026 .

For questions, please contact: Juan Manuel Borrero or Ivan Milic (borrero@leibniz-kis.de; milic@leibniz-kis.de)

KIS is a foundation under public law of the State of Baden-Württemberg. Its mission is to conduct fundamental astrophysical research with a focus on solar physics. Current research foci are (1) Solar Magnetism, (2) Solar-Stellar connections, and (3) Instruments, techniques, and data. KIS participates in several EU cooperation projects and contributes advanced instrumentation to the DKIST 4-m solar telescope on Maui, USA.

You can expect a challenging and future-oriented field of activity with opportunities for creativity at an innovative and successful research institute, a wide range of development and training opportunities, and an open and constructive working atmosphere, together with the social benefits customary in the public sector. title: 3D Motion Evaluator (Human Motion & Physical Plausibility)
description:
About Turing:

Turing is one of the world’s fastest-growing AI companies, accelerating the advancement and deployment of powerful AI systems.

Turing helps customers in two ways: Working with the world’s leading AI labs to advance frontier model capabilities in thinking, reasoning, coding, agentic behavior, multimodality, multilinguality, STEM and frontier knowledge; and leveraging that work to build real-world AI systems that solve mission-critical priorities for companies.

Role Overview:

We are seeking detail-oriented evaluators to support the evaluation and benchmarking of 2D and 3D embodied AI agents. In this role, you will review human animation sequences to assess movement naturalness, physical plausibility, and consistency. You will identify animation artifacts and apply standardized ratings based on the severity, frequency, and persistence of observed issues.

What You’ll Do

  • Review 2D and 3D human animations for natural movement and physical plausibility.
  • Assess foot placement, body balance, center-of-mass movement, and anatomical joint positioning.
  • Identify motion artifacts, including foot sliding, joint jitter, joint pops, body intersections, floating body parts, and unnatural poses.
  • Evaluate the severity, frequency, and persistence of movement inconsistencies throughout each clip.
  • Assign ratings on a 1–5 scale using provided guidelines, ranging from natural human motion to catastrophic motion.
  • Distinguish between minor, noticeable, persistent, and severe motion artifacts.
  • Evaluate each clip as a whole, avoiding the lowest rating solely because an agent pauses during a quiet moment.
  • Maintain accuracy, focus, and consistent judgment across multiple animation sequences.

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Strong visual observation skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to distinguish natural from unnatural human movements and body positions.
  • Understanding of basic human anatomy, joint movement, and physical motion.
  • Ability to recognize common animation artifacts and physical inconsistencies.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to apply evaluation guidelines consistently.
  • Ability to sustain concentration while reviewing multiple animation sequences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Relevant experience in animation, motion capture, biomechanics, game testing, or visual annotation.
  • Experience evaluating motion quality or applying structured scoring rubrics.

Engagement and Payment

This is a pay-per-task opportunity. Payment will be processed after successful completion and verification of the assigned tasks.

We are looking for a DevOps / Site Reliability Engineer to own the reliability, releases, observability and cost of our production services. You will run multi-cluster Kubernetes workloads, including LLM-powered applications, build automation with modern tooling and AI agents, and keep services fast, secure and stable under peak traffic. We value engineers who automate first, make decisions based on data, respect production, and communicate clearly.

Responsibilities

  • Deploy, scale and operate services on multi-environment, multi-cluster Kubernetes, including disaster recovery failover.
  • Maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines and standardize the release process: versioning, canary, blue-green and automated rollback.
  • Build and run the observability stack (metrics, logs, tracing); define SLIs / SLOs and error budgets and reduce alert noise.
  • Operate LLM applications in production: model latency (TTFT), error rate, rate limiting, model version migration, and token cost monitoring.
  • Participate in on call; lead incident response, root cause analysis and blameless postmortems, and turn the findings into automation or runbooks.
  • Own capacity planning and load testing; evaluate the capacity limits of each layer and tune accordingly.
  • Manage edge and security: CDN caching, WAF / bot protection rules, certificates, access control and compliance remediation; drive supply chain security practices such as image scanning, signing and SBOM.
  • Manage infrastructure and configuration as code (IaC / GitOps) to minimize manual work.
  • Build internal tools and AI agent workflows for releases, health checks, alert triage and root cause analysis, with clear safety guardrails.
  • Drive cost optimization (FinOps): resource quota governance, idle resource cleanup and LLM cost analysis.
  • Write and maintain operational documentation, and collaborate with development, product and platform teams.

Mandatory Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in DevOps / SRE / infrastructure (5+ years for Senior).
  • Solid Linux and networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, TLS, load balancing, reverse proxies); able to troubleshoot production issues independently.
  • Production Kubernetes experience: Deployment / StatefulSet / Service / Ingress, resources and scheduling, HPA, probes and troubleshooting; proficient with Helm.
  • In-depth experience with at least one CI/CD tool (Jenkins / GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / Argo CD, etc.) and a good understanding of Git branching and release strategies.
  • Familiar with the Prometheus ecosystem (PromQL, Alertmanager, Grafana) and experienced in designing SLO-based alerts.
  • Proficient in at least one language for automation: Python / Go / Shell.
  • Experience with on-call and production incident handling; able to write clear postmortem reports.
  • Excellent problem solving, teamwork and communication skills.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience in building AI Infrastructure (e.g RL environment).
  • Daily use of AI coding / ops agents (Claude Code, Copilot, etc.), or experience building automation such as MCP servers IaC / GitOps: Terraform / OpenTofu, Argo CD / Flux, Kustomize; Policy as Code (OPA / Kyverno).
  • Advanced observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, log pipelines (Fluent Bit / Vector), eBPF tooling.
  • Security and compliance: image scanning (Trivy), signing (cosign / Sigstore), SBOM / SLSA, secrets management (Vault, etc.).
  • CDN / WAF experience: caching and security configuration on Akamai, Fastly or Cloudflare.
  • Multi-cluster / multi-AZ disaster recovery, global traffic failover, chaos engineering.
  • Public cloud experience: AWS, Azure or GCP (CKA / CKS or cloud vendor certifications preferred).
  • Database operations basics: monitoring, capacity and backup for MySQL and Redis.
  • Experience keeping high-concurrency services stable under peak traffic.

title: Environmental Technician - Stack Tester in , United States
description:
About Us

Groundbreaker. Game changer. Pioneer.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

TRC's professionals work with a broad range of commercial, industrial and government clients and the communities they serve. We deliver breakthrough solutions that address local needs -- so our clients can better succeed in an ever-changing world.

Working at TRC means tackling interesting, meaningful projects. We pride ourselves on our collaborative spirit, entrepreneurial zeal and agile corporate structure. We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview

Looking to make a difference with your work and create a positive impact on the environment? TRC is seeking an entry-level Environmental Scientist/Technician in the Air Measurements Practice of our Eagan, MN office to assist with performance of air emissions testing projects at various industrial facilities.

Our projects help industry achieve environmental compliance while maintaining productivity. Join a great team of established professionals who will show you the ropes of an exciting career in air quality.

This is an excellent opportunity to develop or expand a professional career. TRC values safety, ethics and integrity, and offers the ability to develop or expand meaningful work for a range of clients.

Responsibilities

Under supervision, set up equipment and collect samples at facility emissions sources that may require working at heights, indoors and outdoors in all weather conditions, including but not limited to: heat, cold, humidity, snow, rain, wind, direct sunlight, and noise.
Projects involve a considerable amount of overnight travel, generally in the Midwest; however, projects may be all over the United States. The field-testing portion of each project typically lasts from 1 to 5 days and the test teams are generally home on the weekends, but some projects may require working or traveling on a weekend. The number of people needed in the field and the number of days in the field, varies with each project and changes from week to week. Expect 75% of the weeks to involve field work.
During testing, the Environmental Scientist will be at the location recording data, operating equipment, or working in the trailer recovering samples, performing analysis, etc.
When not in the field, duties may include equipment calibrations and repairs, prep and packing for future projects, vehicle maintenance, basic sample analysis and tasks of that nature.
The Environmental Scientist will become proficient in the various EPA sampling methods and develop knowledge about many types of industrial processes.
The experienced Environmental Scientist typically advances into either a client-oriented career path of project management and business development or into a technical oriented career path working with the latest monitoring and analytical equipment.
Qualifications

description:

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. **Posted Job Title**

Research Specialist C

**Job Profile Title**

Research Specialist C

**Job Description Summary**

The Leung Lab consists of biologists, clinicians, and computational scientists working together to study how skin and other organs respond to injury and inflammation, with the ultimate goal of improving patient outcomes. We focus on understanding the molecular drivers of scar formation, unraveling the mechanisms driving skin diseases, identifying prognostic and predictive biomarkers to improve clinical diagnosis, and discovering new treatments to enable personalized medicine.

The purpose of this position is to perform research to study human granulomatous diseases. The ideal individual will have a bachelors or equivalent degree and at least 5 years of post-doctoral experience preferred in biology, including mouse and in vitro models. The individual should also be willing to work in a highly collaborative environment to support ongoing projects in the laboratory, train lab members, and independently design/coordinate/execute research studies in consultation with the PI.

**Job Description**

**Job Responsibilities**

- Mouse husbandry and survival surgeries
- Human skin cell culture
- Oral and written presentation of work, including lab notebook maintenance, assistance with manuscripts and grant applications
- Other duties and responsibilities as assigned

**Duties**

The purpose of this position is to perform research to study mammalian tissue regeneration and inflammatory skin diseases. The ideal individual will have a bachelor’s degree and at least 3-5 years’ experience in developmental biology and gene regulation, including animal models, flow cytometry, core molecular biology techniques (cloning, PCR, qPCR, chromatin immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, ELISA), and genomics approaches (RNA-Seq, exome sequencing, ATAC-Seq). The individual should have a strong computation background to analyze data sets from genomics studies. The individual should also be willing to work in a highly collaborative environment to support ongoing projects in the laboratory, train lab members, independently design/coordinate/execute research studies in consultation with the PI, and help in preparing manuscripts, presentations, and grant applications.

**Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree and at least 3-5 years experience in gene regulation, inflammation, skin biology or related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience are required. The preferred candidate will have at least 3 years of experience working in the field of skin biology, as well as outstanding oral and written communication skills. The highly preferred candidate will have a proven record of first-author publications, management and technical skills in leading a small research group, and the ability to regularly review and maintain research records for a research group.

Masters or Ph.D in biology preferred.

This position is contingent upon funding.

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Perelman School of Medicine

If you apply when you’re newly hired, you won’t have to provide proof of good health or be subject to underwriting requirements. Eligible family members must always provide proof of good health and are subject to underwriting.

Take advantage of the University’s libraries and athletic facilities, or visit our arboretum and art galleries. title: Flight Telecom Systems Engineer III
description:
## **Job Details**

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

**Responsibilities:**

The **JPL Communications and Instruments Division** perform scientific investigations, advanced technology research, engineering developments and system implementations encompassing space telecommunications, tracking and active remote sensing using electromagnetic waves.

The **Flight Communications and Tracking Section** provides cost-effective space communications systems, software defined radios, high power RF amplifiers, and power supplies that support primary telecom subsystems and major radar and radiometer science payloads. The section also provides Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) flight equipment, radiometric science instruments, high stability frequency standards and clocks and seismometers for NASA/JPL missions. In addition to flight hardware expertise, the section specializes in collection of and processing of worldwide, fixed site, GNSS data that is processed into clock, atmospheric, and ionospheric GNSS correction metrics.  The section also develops high stability frequency references and clocks for flight and ground applications.

The Flight Communications & Tracking Section at JPL is looking for a highly motivated and experienced **Flight Telecom Systems Engineer III** to join their Communication System Engineering and Operations Group. As a member of this Group, you will have an opportunity to be involved in all phases of product development from early concept and mission formulation, low technology readiness specification and prototyping to engineering and flight model development and implementation, functional and environmental testing, and flight operations support. In this role, you will perform complex and wide-ranging engineering tasks across the telecom discipline and its interfaces, exercising increasing independence across the product lifecycle.

**Tasks include but are not limited to:**

- Provide telecom system engineering support on flight telecom subsystems for deep-space, Earth-orbiting, and lunar/Mars relay missions. Generate telecom component and subsystem requirements with flow-down, and verify multifunctional telecom requirements for consistency across interfacing subsystems.
- Conduct system-level link analyses using statistically derived link parameters. Independently evaluate telecom components, algorithms, systems, and end-to-end performance, identifying improvements and risks.
- Apply advanced principles to interpret complex telecom and tracking data and test results. Research subsystem data to inform architecture and risk decisions, partnering with project personnel on risk mitigation plans.
- Lead infusion of new technology into flight telecom products, documenting requirements, progress, and test results. Develop critical technical models for improved multifunctional telecom products.
- Partner with engineers and project personnel on cross-discipline trade studies and analyses of alternatives. Provide telecom support to Team X concurrent design and to mission and concept proposal teams, including formal proposal writing and review.
- Plan, maintain, and document mass, power, and data volume allocations, resolving cross-component conflicts. Perform or independently review reliability analyses (worst-case, parts stress, radiation, thermal, structural) and interface failure mode analysis.
- Draft or update telecom functional description documents, comm behavior manager documents, and design control documents such as ICDs, requirements, test reports, and design description documents.
- Create detailed test plans, procedures, and reports aligned with V&V objectives. Develop critical V&V plans and verify requirements. Support key spacecraft-level ATLO tests: subsystem functional, ground-station compatibility, and environmental testing.
- Collaborate with ground station providers: DSN, NSN, ESTRACK, and commercial providers (e.g., KSAT).

- Support the product manager on risks, performance error budgets, trade studies, design integration, and delivery schedules. Present technical status and results at management, project, and design reviews.
- Serve as a real-time telecom operations engineer across all mission phases (launch, cruise, critical events, extended operations), monitoring subsystem health, performance, and link status.
- Support DSN, NSN, and commercial pass planning and execution, including command verification, telemetry acquisition, and link performance against pre-pass predicts. Participate in shift coverage, performing real-time and post-pass assessment and flagging off-nominal performance.
- Support telecom anomaly response, performing root-cause analysis and recommending corrective actions with the flight team.
- Lead a telecom operations team supporting one or more flight projects, coordinating shift, pass, staffing, and on-call coverage. Serve as telecom operations lead for operations readiness reviews, ORTs, and sequence/command reviews.
- Coordinate telecom operations with subsystem leads, the mission operations team, and project management. Train, qualify, and certify telecom operations engineers on mission-specific procedures, tools, and flight rules.
- Develop and maintain telecom operations products, including flight rules, SOPs, contingency and anomaly procedures, and operations handbooks. Capture flight operations lessons learned into updated procedures, tools, and training.
- Design and implement software tools and dashboards (e.g., Python, Jupyter, MATLAB) to automate telemetry trending, limit checking, and anomaly detection, and to compare downlink/uplink telemetry against link budget predicts, flagging deviations.
- Mentor junior engineers and interns. Demonstrate a collaborative, safety-conscious, team-oriented approach, and build working relationships across the telecom team and with other subsystem engineers.
- Take ownership of assigned tasks and deliverables. Communicate progress, risks, and recommendations to senior engineers, task leads, and stakeholders, and contribute to planning, scheduling, and technical reviews.

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s in Electrical, Electronics, Computer Hardware Engineering, Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a similar technical discipline with a minimum of 6 years of related work experience; Masters in a similar discipline with a minimum of 4 years of related work experience; PhD in a similar discipline with a minimum of 2 years of related work experience.
- Excellent communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills, including interacting with project, program, and line management, the engineering team, other NASA centers, and other agencies. Frequent interaction with industry partners, initiating cross-organizational collaboration as needed.
- Demonstrated ownership of a task, product, or small effort, including coordinating other engineers. Growing leadership experience, such as mentoring junior engineers/interns, leading a task or analysis, or representing a team in technical reviews. As a team lead, accountable for performance, schedule, and budget.
- Ability to balance and prioritize multiple tasks, identify and communicate schedule or technical risk, and adapt to frequent plan changes in a rapid-pace concurrent engineering environment.
- Demonstrated sound engineering judgment and reliability, with increasing scope and independence. Works independently with limited direction, resolves highly complex technical problems, and shows creativity and innovative thinking on critical issues.
- Proven experience designing, implementing, and testing electronic hardware for complex spaceflight systems. Strong background in RF systems, Software-Defined Radios, digital and analog hardware, and embedded software/firmware.
- Proficiency in Python, Jupyter Notebook, and MATLAB for system analysis and automation. Hands-on experience with RF test equipment, such as spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, noise figure meters, and bit error rate testers.
- Hands-on system testing experience, including test planning, procedure development, and data analysis, and the ability to debug and troubleshoot complex systems. Experience within a multidisciplinary systems engineering (telecom, radar, spacecraft, avionics) or test team (electrical integration, spacecraft assembly electrical, functional, or telecom compatibility).
- Experience designing telecom subsystems for space applications, managing link budgets, and reducing link uncertainties. Knowledge of processes used to verify and validate system design requirements.
- Ability to support domestic and international travel for testing and mission support.

**Preferred Skills:**

- Knowledge of Laboratory, NASA, and government policies, procedures, and regulations.
- Direct experience with flight telecom component development and delivery.
- Understanding of advanced telecom principles, including modulation and coding, antennas and RF front ends, link design and modeling, networking, and radio test automation.
- Experience with SPICE kernels for spacecraft trajectory modeling in telecom link analysis.
- Proficiency with tools for numerical analysis, electronic design, firmware, embedded software, and/or test automation.
- Familiarity with requirements management systems such as Jama.
- Experience with cost estimation for spacecraft components and subsystems.
- Familiarity with ground station providers, including DSN, NSN, ESTRACK, and commercial providers (e.g., KSAT).
- Experience with spectral mask regulations and measurement techniques.
- Experience with multipath and ray-tracing analysis for base-station-to-rover communication links.
- Experience developing, documenting, and executing radio system tests, with formal V&V requirements tracking.
- Experience designing and testing Software Defined Radios (SDR).

title: HR Service Center Coordinator
description:
**Job Description:**

Provide outstanding customer service by serving as the point of contact for intermediate level employee inquiries through in person, phone, or email at the HR Service Center. Responsible for assisting new hires, including faculty, staff, and student workers, in on-boarding business processes, and ensuring the associated HR data is complete, accurate, and compliant. Provide information on policies, processes, and programs across a broad range of HR topics, including employment, benefits, and payroll. By possessing a comprehensive knowledge of the department’s offerings and policies, the HR Service Center Coordinator will be able to contribute to the overall efficient operation of the HR Service Center.

## **Major Responsibilities:**

**1. Provide excellent customer service to all faculty, staff and students in person, on the phone and by email.**

- Provide the Brown community with information about and assistance with: HR policies and procedures, benefits, payroll, and Workday self-service assistance.
- Evaluate and resolve simple to complex issues, using relatively thorough knowledge of functional areas’ policies and procedures, systems, and internal processes. The goal is to answer the question or resolve the issue at the initial contact.
- Escalate high-level inquiries and issues by engaging with the appropriate functional area specialists or departments.
- Manage the effective resolution of customer issues by thoroughly researching the issue or question.
- Possess intermediate knowledge of employment among faculty and staff, including union and nonunion staff, full and part-time employees, seasonal and intermittent employees, and research and teaching employees.
- Maintain working knowledge of payroll processing and schedules. Including payroll processes related to non-US citizens.
- Ensure all employees are aware of how to access to employee benefit plans information, and summary plan descriptions.
- Respond to benefits related questions and issues.
- Provide support and coordination for special events and projects.
- Provide recommendations or suggest methods to update, simplify, and enhance, processes and procedures.

**2. Review and approve employee self-service onboarding in Workday and related business processes to ensure a smooth onboarding of faculty, staff, and students. In addition, review and approve other core employee business processes.**

- Ensure the onboarding process in Workday is completed and correct for all new hires.
- Review, and approve as needed, all Workday business processes related to onboarding and HR core data for all faculty, students, and staff.
- Ensure employee and student worker records are complete and accurate, and employment processes are effectively launched and tracked.
- Adhere to the federal Form I-9 regulations and processes.
- Confirm all benefit related information is entered and correct in Workday.

**3. Audit and monitor HR core data and provide general UHR support.**

- Run audit reports according to established protocol and data standards.
- Reach out to, and follow up with, faculty, students, and staff, to obtain missing or updated information.
- Assist employees accessing The Work Number to facilitate their own employment verifications. Respond to all written and verbal verification of employment requests for employees that cannot be completed through The Work Number.
- Provide HR information and support as requested to other departments (i.e., Office of the General Counsel, the Insurance Office, the Loan Office, etc.).

## **Education and Experience:**

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education & experience.
- The ideal candidate will have a minimum of two years of related experience in an HR customer service role,

- Strong organization skills and great attention to detail, a keen ability to prioritize and multi-task, and an ability to adhere to and meet deadlines.
- High level of interpersonal skills to handle sensitive and confidential situations and documentation and excellent communication skills (oral, written and presentation).
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications including Excel.

title: Senior Software/Data Engineer, Bot Detection (EMEA)
description:
At Hugging Face, we're on a journey to democratize good AI. We are building the fastest growing platform for AI builders with over 20 million users who collectively shared over 4 million models, 1 million datasets & 1.5 million apps. Our open-source libraries have more than 700,000 stars on Github.

**About the Role**

Hugging Face hosts millions of models, datasets and Spaces, and serves a very large community of developers. With that scale comes automated abuse: fake accounts, scraping, spam, and bots gaming downloads, likes and trending signals. We're building a small, dedicated bot-detection effort inside our Trust & Safety team, and we're looking for an engineer to own the data and modeling side of it.

You'll turn large volumes of traffic, account and behavioral data into reliable decisions about what is human, what is automated, and what is abusive. You'll work hand-in-hand with our signals-focused bot-detection engineer, from raw telemetry all the way to production detection and enforcement.

#### What you'll do

- Build and run detection pipelines on large-scale traffic and activity data (requests, sessions, accounts, repo interactions, API usage)
- Develop and deploy detection models and heuristics: anomaly detection, clustering of coordinated activity, graph-based approaches, supervised classifiers where labels exist
- Define features from client and network signals together with the signals engineer, and measure how robust they are as attackers adapt
- Build the feedback loops: labeling, evaluation, false-positive monitoring, dashboards, alerting
- Investigate live campaigns end-to-end (fake account waves, metric inflation, large-scale scraping) and turn what you learn into durable detections
- Keep things proportionate and privacy-respecting, and minimize impact on legitimate users and automated-but-legitimate workloads (CI, research crawlers, integrations)

- You have strong experience applying data science or ML to adversarial problems in production: bot detection, fraud, abuse, spam, security analytics or similar
- You're fluent in Python and SQL, and comfortable with large-scale data tooling (Spark, ClickHouse, BigQuery, or similar)
- You've taken models or detection logic from exploration to production and kept them working over time
- You understand web traffic and network data well enough to reason about what a signal really means and how it can be spoofed
- You think in terms of precision/recall trade-offs, attacker adaptation and operational cost, not just offline metrics
- You're pragmatic, autonomous, and you enjoy working closely with one or two people in a fast-moving team

**Nice to have**

- Published work on bot detection, web measurement or adversarial ML (a PhD is welcome but not required, as long as you want your work running in prod)
- Experience with graph analytics or streaming detection
- Familiarity with the ML/open-source ecosystem and the Hugging Face Hub

**One more thing**

At Hugging Face we believe great AI shouldn't require a massive cluster, we build for everyone, especially the GPU-poor. And because we read every application, here's a small sign that you read this one too: start your answer to the first application question with the words “GPU-poor and proud 🤗”. No trick, no catch, it just tells us a real person is on the other side.

**More about Hugging Face**

**We are actively working to build a culture that values diversity, equity, and inclusivity**. We are intentionally building a workplace where people feel respected and supported—regardless of who you are or where you come from. We believe this is foundational to building a great company and community. Hugging Face is an equal opportunity employer and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

**We value development.** You will work with some of the smartest people in our industry. We are an organization that has a bias for impact and is always challenging ourselves to continuously grow. We provide all employees with reimbursement for relevant conferences, training, and education.

**We care about your well-being.** We offer flexible working hours and remote options. We offer health, dental, and vision benefits for employees and their dependents. We also offer parental leave and flexible paid time off.

**We support our employees wherever they are**. While we have office spaces in NYC and Paris, we're very distributed and all remote employees have the opportunity to visit our offices. If needed, we'll also outfit your workstation to ensure you succeed.

**We want our teammates to be shareholders**. All employees have company equity as part of their compensation package. If we succeed in becoming a category-defining platform in machine learning and artificial intelligence, everyone enjoys the upside.

**We support the community**. We believe major scientific advancements are the result of collaboration across the field. Join a community supporting the ML/AI community.

The team works closely with clients at every stage of their journey, helping them navigate challenges, avoid financial pitfalls, and implement practical solutions before, during, and after major transformational projects or transactions creating lasting impact.

Shape the people agenda behind transformative deals-helping clients navigate the talent, culture, and organizational changes that make M&A work. As a consultant, you'll turn complex challenges into practical solutions and grow alongside a collaborative team at the center of high-impact transactions.

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/24/2026

Work You'll Do

As an M&A Human Capital Consultant on the Integration & Divestiture team, you will:
  • Conduct Human Capital due diligence across compensation, benefits, human resources (HR) compliance, labor relations, HR communications, operations and technology, talent, and culture; identify transaction risks and opportunities.
  • Support organizational change management programs, including impact assessments, stakeholder and employee engagement, leadership enablement, and transaction communications.
  • Assess legacy cultures, define future-state culture objectives, and develop plans to support cultural alignment.
  • Support integration of human resources functions, including HR systems, service delivery, total rewards, payroll, leadership development, and talent strategy.
  • Support organizational design, workforce transition, and workforce optimization initiatives for combined, separated, or transformed organizations.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams

  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The Team

Within Deloitte's M&A offering, the Integration & Divestiture - Human Capital team helps clients address the people-related dimensions of transactions across the deal lifecycle. The team supports organizations through diligence, pre-close planning, Day 1 readiness, integration, and separation by focusing on areas such as organization design, workforce transition, employee communications, change management, and human resources operating model decisions. Working alongside cross-functional deal teams, the practice helps clients manage workforce risks, support business continuity, and execute human capital priorities that enable transaction value.

  • Experience executing project plans with defined milestones and deadlines and collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders.

Identify delivery risks early and communicate clearly with stakeholders when priorities, scope, or timelines need adjustment. Provide Technical Leadership

Guide technical discussions and help the team evaluate architectural approaches and engineering trade-offs.

Partner with senior engineers and architects on technical strategy and long-term platform evolution.

Dive into complex technical issues when necessary and work alongside engineers during critical production or customer-impacting problems.

Help drive root-cause analysis and ensure corrective and preventive actions are completed following significant incidents. Collaborate Across the Organization

Build strong working relationships with Product Management, Support, L3 Engineering, QA, DevOps/SRE, Architecture, Security, and other engineering teams.

Partner closely with Support and L3 teams to understand customer-impacting issues, prioritize escalations, and ensure timely resolution.

Create effective feedback loops between Engineering, Product, Support, and customers to continuously improve product quality and reliability. Own Operational Excellence

Establish strong ownership of production services within the engineering team.

Partner with operations and engineering teams on monitoring, observability, incident response, capacity planning, and production readiness.

You are the Archeana owner for your country. You decide how the portfolio reaches your market, and you keep the majority of the revenue you collect there. - Build a small local network of ambassadors and delivery partners as you grow.
- Propose new low-touch offerings for your country. The platform is designed to add them easily.

**What we provide**
- A live platform, methodology and product library, with the engineering, operations and infrastructure already in place.
- Shared systems for billing, referrals, reporting and customer data.
- A central team that builds, maintains and improves the products, so you can spend your time on customers.
- Early access to new offerings across the portfolio.
- A path to more. If a business within Archeana grows into its own legal entity, country co-founders who helped build it get first right to participate in that entity.

- Know how buyers in your country actually decide: who signs, what they trust, and how they pay.
- Can open doors, with a network among founders, CXOs, HR and operations leaders, advisers or ecosystem bodies.
- Are comfortable with ambiguity and with building from zero.
- Are resilient to commission-only income in the early months, because that's what revenue-share means.
- Can present credibly in the language of your market.

**What we're being honest about**
- This is revenue-share only: no salary, no guaranteed income and no equity at the outset. You earn from the revenue you collect.
- We're early. Some offerings are still being finalised and launched. We'll tell you exactly what is live and what is not, and we won't oversell it to your customers either.
- The agreement will be a contractual partnership. We'll agree a local legal setup that suits your country.

**How to apply**
Send a message or comment Country with your country, your background in three lines, and the first customer segment you would go after. We'll reply with a short call invitation and the full seat terms.

*One seat per country. Seats open on a rolling basis.*

(Eligibility Rules Apply) If this sounds like the right nonprofit opportunity for you, apply today!


ABOUT BOYS & GIRLS CLUB OF CHICOPEE

Everything we do at the Boys & Girls Club of Chicopee is done with one goal in mind: to help every child achieve success. With roots dating all the way back to 1860, we have remained steadfast in our mission to help kids thrive. We provide youth from ages 5 to 18 with a safe place to develop themselves and form connections with their peers. Our staff leads regular programs and activities that encourage positive development within the areas of academic success, healthy lifestyles, and good character and citizenship. We strive to create an environment where every child can prosper!

Every employee is important here because every person makes a direct impact on our members. We foster a family-like atmosphere where everyone feels comfortable expressing themselves and having a good time. At our core, we are about having fun and helping each other. We are incredibly thankful for our awesome team, which is why we offer generous benefits and an amazing work culture.


A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A FULL TIME NUTRITION COORDINATOR

As the Full-Time Nutrition Coordinator, you will oversee the daily operations of the Club's food and nutrition programs, ensuring that children and teens have access to nutritious meals and snacks in a safe, welcoming environment. Under the direction of the Program Systems & Data Manager, you will plan, coordinate, implement, and monitor food service programs in accordance with requirements established by the Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE), the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Public Health (DPH).

You will take the lead in managing the Club's after-school, evening, and summer food service programs, including the Summer Food Service Program (SFSP), Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), and other nutrition initiatives as assigned. This includes developing monthly meal menus, coordinating food purchasing and deliveries, preparing and serving meals, and ensuring that all meals and snacks meet applicable nutritional and program requirements. You will also ensure menus are posted and accessible to families and staff, and that members with special dietary needs are appropriately accommodated and communicated to staff.

Beyond meal service, you will help make nutrition education an engaging part of the Club experience. Working collaboratively with Program System & Data Manger, Site Managers and Youth Development Professionals, you will develop and implement hands-on activities that encourage healthy eating, food awareness, and positive lifestyle choices for youth ages 5-18.

You will be responsible for maintaining clean, sanitary, and organized kitchen and food storage areas, ensuring equipment and supplies are properly maintained, and monitoring food safety practices. Regular site visits will be conducted to observe food service operations, ensure compliance with program regulations, and identify opportunities for improvement.

Accurate documentation and organization are essential to this position. You will maintain required program records, compile and verify participation and meal service data, and prepare reports to support program accountability and compliance. You will also assist with training and supervising staff assigned to kitchen operations and participate in required professional development and program-related meetings.

As a member of the Club's larger youth development team, you may also step into a Youth or Teen Development Professional role when needed. You will serve as a positive role model, encourage member participation, and help create a safe, supportive environment where all young people can thrive.


QUALIFICATIONS FOR A NUTRITION COORDINATOR

  • Associates Degree Required or a minimum of three (3) years equilivent combination of education, training and experience in a non-profit organization in the area of youth development, nutrition and/or elementary or secondary education is preferred
  • Experience working with youth and teens, ages 5-18 years of age
  • Knowledge of youth development
  • Nutrition and food service experience required preferably in the area of youth service
  • ServSafe certified, or willing to obtain within the first 6 months of employment
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Publisher and Word in particular)
  • Computer literacy, including database management
  • Communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Ability to plan and implement quality training programs
  • Ability to organize and supervise members in a safe environment
  • Must be deemed suitable after initial and subsequent Background Record Checks
  • Mandatory CPR, First Aid Certification
  • Must be 21 years or older
  • Valid Driver' License and acceptable MVR check

Do you have strong conflict resolution skills? Can you think on your feet and quickly solve problems? Are you highly observant? If yes, you might just be perfect for this nonprofit position!


WORK SCHEDULE FOR A PART-TIME YOUTH DEVELOPMENT PROFESSIONAL

This is a full-time position with a schedule that supports the Club Youth and Teen After School and Evening Programs during the academic year and transitions to a varied schedule during the summer months to accommodate Summer Program operations.

Company Overview

Continuum Associates (CA) is a leading power systems and energy consulting firm dedicated to delivering innovative solutions in power system planning and operations, grid optimization, renewable integration, energy market analysis, and regulatory compliance. Our expertise helps electric power utilities and Independent System Operators (ISOs) navigate the complexities of the evolving energy landscape, ensuring reliable, efficient, and sustainable operations. Our team brings over 200 years of combined industry experience, and we specialize in renewable energy integration, advanced power system modeling and studies, transmission and distribution grid planning and operations, and technical and strategy consulting across the electrical energy and power systems ecosystem.

We are seeking a dynamic Product Manager and Product Owner who will drive the growth and expansion of our software and SaaS ecosystems, which have been used by over 100 utilities and electric infrastructure developers over the past decade.

About the Position

We are seeking a highly motivated and hands-on Product Manager / Product Owner to lead the end-to-end lifecycle of our software products — from concept and design to development, launch, and iteration. This role requires a mix of strategic thinking, technical fluency, and execution excellence. This role requires someone who is strategic yet hands-on, capable of working in a fast-moving startup environment with minimal resources and maximum accountability. Our products are purpose-built software for the energy and power sector, grounded in electrical engineering and used by utility engineers, grid planners, grid system operators, independent power producers, and project developers. You must be sharp enough to pick up the nuances of the power systems domain quickly and to speak credibly with the engineers who build, use, and evaluate our products.

Key Responsibilities

Define and maintain the product vision, strategy, and roadmap, ensuring alignment with company goals and client needs as well as industry standards and the evolving needs of the power and energy sector.
Conduct market and user research to identify new opportunities, assess competitive trends and landscape, and propose new product ideas.
Learn and adapt quickly to our industry and the electrical power systems domain (such as transmission and distribution planning, grid operations, and engineering studies and analysis workflows), understand the landscape and unmet client needs of utility engineers, grid planners, and operators, and identify where product and data-driven opportunities exist.
Partner closely with in-house power systems domain experts and developers to translate engineering concepts, study methodologies, industry standards, and utility workflows into product requirements, and help validate that features, calculations, and outputs are technically sound and meet engineering expectations.
Write clear, detailed, and structured product requirements (PRDs) and user stories with well-defined acceptance criteria. Think through feature interdependencies, user flows, and technical implications, including the engineering logic and data inputs behind domain-specific features, to ensure completeness and feasibility.
Act as the bridge between business, design, software development, and engineering teams and power systems domain experts — ensuring clarity of goals, priorities, and deliverables.
Maintain strong awareness of the

technology landscape

and emerging innovations; communicate effectively with technical teams about feasibility, architecture, and implementation trade-offs.
Track developments in power system standards, regulations, and market rules (for example, those of ISOs/RTOs and reliability organizations) and assess their impact on product direction and roadmap priorities.
Own the product backlog and sprint planning using tools. Gather and analyze user feedback and usage data to inform the roadmap and prioritization.
You should be proficient in product development tools like JIRA, Trello, Confluence, Figma and other similar platforms/tools.
Be a

hands-on contributor

who can roll up their sleeves to fill gaps, coordinate execution, or test early prototypes when needed to ensure timely delivery.
Engage directly with clients and users, including electrical engineers at utilities, system operators, and project developers, to understand needs, present product demos, gather feedback, and translate insights into enhancements.
Lead technical conversations during product evaluations, pilots, and proposal or bid responses: explain how the products address engineering use cases, answer technical questions credibly, and capture client feedback to shape the roadmap.
Define and track product KPIs and success metrics to evaluate performance and outcomes.

Qualifications & Skills

At a minimum, a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or Computer Science. A degree in electrical engineering, specifically in electrical power systems, is a strong plus, though not required, as it helps you understand our products in depth, work effectively with development and domain teams to manage the roadmap and development process, and speak credibly with client electrical engineers evaluating our products.
An MBA is a plus.
7+ years of experience in product management, product ownership for software or SaaS products, preferably B2B or enterprise software for technical users. Proven prior history of success as a Product Manager and in bringing SaaS tools to the market.
Proven proficiency with JIRA, Trello, Figma, Confluence, or equivalent tools for managing requirements and workflows.
Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) and agile methodologies.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to write detailed requirements and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to understand new industries quickly and absorb the technical nuances of complex engineering domains, engage with clients, and propose innovative product solutions.
Experience with engineering, analytical, or energy-sector software is an advantage.
Ability to hold credible, technically informed conversations with electrical engineers at utilities, system operators, and developers who are evaluating the product, including demos, pilots, and technical Q&A.
Technical aptitude and intellectual curiosity to pick up power systems concepts (for example, grid planning, interconnection, operations, and related engineering studies) and to ask the right questions of developers and domain experts, without needing to be an electrical engineer.
Self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, resource-constrained, startup-type environment and delivers high-quality results with minimal supervision.
Strong problem-solving, analytical, and prioritization skills.

What Success Looks Like

You manage the product end-to-end — from idea to launch — with clear documentation, predictable execution, and measurable impact.
You communicate seamlessly across business, design, and technology functions.
You deliver value quickly, handle ambiguity confidently, and take initiative beyond your job scope to move the product forward.
Clients and internal teams view you as a trusted product leader who blends strategic thinking with operational excellence.
You quickly build enough domain depth to lead roadmap and design discussions with developers and domain experts, and to hold technically credible conversations with client engineers evaluating the product.
Complete ownership of our suite of software tools and SaaS platform. The buck stops with you.

title: Information Cyber Security Analyst
description:
We're Hiring | Information & Cyber Security Analyst

Experience: 5–10 Years

Department: Information Technology / Information Security

Employment Type: Full-Time

Location: Gurgaon India (Remote)

We are looking for a skilled and proactive Information & Cyber Security Analyst to strengthen our information security operations. The ideal candidate will be responsible for monitoring security threats, investigating incidents, managing vulnerabilities, reviewing identity and access controls, and supporting continuous improvement of the organisation's cybersecurity posture.

The candidate should have hands-on experience with security monitoring tools, incident management, vulnerability assessment and Microsoft security technologies.

Key Responsibilities

1. Security Monitoring & Threat Detection

  • Monitor and analyse security alerts from SIEM, EDR/MDR platforms, firewalls, identity management systems and Microsoft Defender.
  • Identify suspicious activities, potential threats, unusual login patterns and security vulnerabilities.
  • Investigate security alerts and distinguish genuine threats from false positives.
  • Maintain continuous visibility of the organisation's security environment.

2. Security Incident Response

  • Investigate and respond to phishing attacks, malware infections, compromised accounts, suspicious authentication activities and other cybersecurity incidents.
  • Support incident containment, investigation, remediation and recovery activities.
  • Escalate critical security incidents to relevant stakeholders and ensure timely resolution.
  • Maintain detailed incident records, investigation findings and lessons learned.

3. Vulnerability Management

  • Review vulnerability assessment and security scanning reports.
  • Validate identified vulnerabilities and prioritise critical and high-risk findings.
  • Coordinate with IT infrastructure, application and support teams to ensure timely patching and remediation.
  • Track remediation progress and maintain an updated vulnerability register.

4. Identity & Access Management

  • Review user access rights, privileged accounts and administrator permissions.
  • Identify excessive privileges, dormant accounts and inappropriate access.
  • Monitor suspicious authentication activities and unusual login behaviour.
  • Support periodic access reviews and ensure compliance with access management policies.

5. Information Security Education & Awareness

  • Support organisation-wide information security awareness and education programmes.
  • Monitor employee participation and completion of mandatory security training.
  • Follow up with employees and managers on overdue training.
  • Initiate the appropriate escalation process for non-compliance.

6. Security Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain security metrics, incident registers, vulnerability trackers and management dashboards.
  • Prepare periodic security reports highlighting risks, incidents and remediation status.
  • Analyse security trends and recommend improvements to existing controls and processes.
  • Support internal and external security audits and compliance requirements.

7. Security Tickets & Service Requests

  • Take ownership of security-related tickets and service requests.
  • Monitor the security ticketing system and respond to requests for security advice, guidance and approvals.
  • Provide timely recommendations and ensure requests are appropriately assessed, documented and resolved.
  • Coordinate with relevant IT and business stakeholders for closure of security-related requests.

Required Skills & Technical Expertise

  • Hands-on experience with SIEM platforms and security monitoring tools.
  • Good working knowledge of EDR/MDR solutions and Microsoft Defender.
  • Understanding of firewalls, endpoint security, network security and threat detection.
  • Experience in cybersecurity incident investigation and response.
  • Knowledge of vulnerability assessment, remediation and patch management.
  • Understanding of Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), identity and access management.
  • Knowledge of phishing, malware, ransomware and other common cyber threats.
  • Experience with security ticketing systems, incident registers and reporting dashboards.
  • Good understanding of information security policies, controls and best practices.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication and documentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications & Certifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity or a related discipline.
  • Relevant certifications such as:
  • CompTIA Security+
  • Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
  • Certified Information Security Manager (CISM)
  • Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH)
  • Microsoft Security certifications (SC-200, SC-300 or equivalent)

Experience Required

  • 5–10 years of relevant experience in Information Security, Cybersecurity Operations, Security Monitoring or IT Security.
  • Practical experience in security incident investigation, vulnerability management and security operations.
  • Experience working in a Microsoft-based enterprise IT environment will be an advantage.

What We Are Looking For

A hands-on cybersecurity professional who can independently monitor security operations, investigate incidents, coordinate remediation activities and work collaboratively with IT and business teams to strengthen the organisation's overall information security framework.

Role Overview

As a Program Manager, the role translates priorities into executable plans and drives the cross-functional delivery needed to achieve and sustain results. The position develops integrated roadmaps, establishes fit-for-purpose governance, drives cross-functional execution, resolves barriers, and maintains accountability from planning through implementation, adoption, benefits realization, and sustainment.

Working across executive Sponsors, business owners, functional teams, project leaders, and partners, the Program Manager influences without direct authority and provides decision-ready visibility into progress, risks, dependencies, resource needs, and outcomes.

  • Protect confidential and proprietary company information.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Communication and Facilitation Skills

  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills.

  • Ability to prepare executive-ready reporting, frame tradeoffs, facilitate complex discussions, and translate program information into clear decisions and actions.

Analytical and Execution Skills

  • Ability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative information, identify risks and dependencies, evaluate options, establish meaningful measures, and drive corrective action through sustained outcomes.

  • Strong knowledge of organizational health and effectiveness, assessment interpretation, root-cause analysis, priority setting, and translating quantitative and qualitative insights into focused opportunities.

Intervention and Portfolio Management Skills

  • Demonstrated ability to design organizational-effectiveness interventions, integrate business-owned initiatives into a coherent portfolio, establish executive governance, and drive Sponsors and owners against commitments.

  • Experience defining outcome measures, monitoring adoption and implementation, facilitating recovery actions, and sustaining improvements through leadership routines, reinforcement, and benefits realization.

Education and Experience

  • PMP, PgMP, Prosci, CCMP, Lean Six Sigma, organizational development, people analytics, or comparable credential preferred.
