title: Research Project Manager
description:
**Department:** MED-Impact Institute

**Salary/Grade:** EXS/7

_Target hiring range for this position will be between 63,080 - 75,000 per year.  Offered salary will be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data._

**Job Summary:**

Manages all activities associated with biomedical &/or social-behavioral research studies considered very complex by the inclusion of several of the following: multiple investigators, teams, sites, sub-contracts, participants, longitudinal assessments/ interventions; &/or multi-million dollar budgets. Ensures completion of contract requirements & client specifications.  Oversees day-to-day operations including identifying & securing needed resources; creating, implementing, monitoring, & updating project plans; facilitating meetings with appropriate parties; tracking tasks/deliverables to ensure timelines, milestones &/or goals are attained; monitoring & reporting progress as appropriate; & resolving or escalating issues in a timely manner.   May co-author scientific papers for presentation & publication & coordinates writing, submission & administration of grants.  Ensures that all study activities are completed by strictly following Good Clinical Practices (GCP) & all current local, state, & federal laws, regulations, guidance, policy & procedure developed by the NU Institutional Review Board (IRB), Food & Drug Administration (FDA) Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), & the International Conference on Harmonization (ICH).

The Recruitment and Retention Project Manager provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for participant recruitment, engagement, and retention for RADAR, a longitudinal biomedical and social-behavioral cohort study of young men who have sex with men and gender-diverse young people. The Manager develops and evaluates integrated recruitment and retention plans, supervises the Recruitment Coordinator, and ensures that outreach and participant engagement activities support study enrollment goals, continued participation, and cohort representation.

Reporting to the RADAR Project Director, the Manager translates study objectives into measurable goals, staffing plans, workflows, and accountable deliverables. This role oversees community partnerships, digital advertising, participant engagement systems, and recruitment and retention performance monitoring. The Manager works closely with study faculty, scheduling and retention staff, biomedical staff, and the data team to identify barriers, improve participant experiences, and resolve operational challenges. All activities must follow approved study protocols, participant consent and contact preferences, University policies, and applicable human subjects research requirements.

This position requires working non-traditional hours multiple times a week, such as evenings and weekends, to attend recruitment events. There is also no guarantee of any regular work from home days given the need to be onsite and out in the community for recruitment and retention purposes.

_Please note:_

Supervisor provides objectives and deadlines.  Work is reviewed for fulfillment of objective and deadlines and overall compliance with policy and procedures.  EE completes some activities without direction, informing supervisor only of potentially controversial matters, and/or far-reaching implications.

_Work Location Requirement_

As this role supports an in-person research study, full-time on-site presence is required. Direct coordination with participants, staff, and study resources must occur on campus to ensure the integrity of study operations and participant engagement. Remote, hybrid, or work-from-home arrangements are not possible for this position.

_Driver’s License Requirement_

Because this position involves the use of a mobile unit to conduct research study visits, applicants must hold a valid driver’s license and meet the eligibility criteria of the University’s Safe Driver Program. This includes following all program guidelines regarding responsibilities, safe driving practices, and authorization for vehicle use on University business.

**Specific Responsibilities**:

_Technical_

- Provides complex scientific & technical leadership in determining research priorities & the plan, design & execution of research projects ensuring that programs of investigation meet specified objectives.
- Plans, develops & implements new processes & protocols to support research studies & maximize/extend study capabilities.
- Oversees completion of study activities per protocol.
- Ensures that study protocols are in compliance with appropriate rules & regulations & reviews study progress and recommends revisions, amendments, and/or other study changes as necessary to better meet needs of sponsors.
- Reviews scientific literature & evaluates & recommends applicable techniques & procedures.

_Administrative_

- Analyzes, evaluates & interprets data to determine relevance to research.
- Assists PI in developing statistical methods & models to analyze & report data based upon study requirements.
- Prepares results & may co-author scientific papers for presentation & publication & disseminates information via seminars, lectures, etc.
- Creates data for use in grant submission & develop new proposals for research including obtaining financial support.
- Acts as liaison between sponsoring agencies, collaborating organizations &/or other research &/or educational institutions.
- Ensures that all study documents associated with current local, state, & federal regulatory guidelines, requirements, laws & research protocols are completed in a timely manner.

_Finance_

- May create &/or manage research study budget which may include deciding on & approving expenditures of funds based on budget.
- Monitors accounts.
- Negotiates prices & specifications with vendors.
- Purchases supplies, materials, equipment & services.
- Ensures appropriate allocation & compliance.
- Invoices study sponsors for study tests/procedures.
- Coordinates & participates in budgetary negotiations with industry sponsors.

_Supervision_

- Trains, directs, assigns duties to & may supervise lab EEs, students, residents &/or fellows.
- Acts as a mentor in regard to education of junior coordinators.

_Miscellaneous_

Performs other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

- Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree in a major such as social or health science or related; OR appropriate combination of education and experience and 5 years' research study or other relevant experience required; OR

- Successful completion of a full course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a master's or higher degree in a major such as social or health science or related; OR appropriate combination of education and experience and 3 years' research study or other relevant experience.

- Supervisory or project management experience required.

- Must complete NU's IRB CITI training before interacting with any participants & must re-certify every 3 years.


**Minimum Competencies: (Skills, knowledge, and abilities.)**

- Project leadership: Ability to translate study objectives into actionable recruitment and retention plans, measurable milestones, staff assignments, and timely deliverables.
- Staff management: Ability to set expectations, delegate effectively, train and coach staff, evaluate performance, and address concerns constructively.
- Recruitment and retention knowledge: Understanding of community outreach, digital recruitment, participant engagement, and longitudinal retention approaches, including barriers affecting adolescents and young adults.
- Data-informed decision-making: Ability to interpret recruitment and retention metrics, distinguish outreach activity from enrollment outcomes, identify performance gaps, and implement and evaluate corrective action.
- Culturally responsive engagement: Ability to build trust and work respectfully with LGBTQ communities, racially and ethnically diverse populations, people living with HIV, and individuals facing stigma or barriers to care.
- Communication and relationship management: Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal skills; ability to develop clear participant-facing communications and maintain productive relationships with staff and community partners.
- Research ethics and confidentiality: Knowledge of human subjects protections, informed consent, privacy, and approved participant contact practices; ability to recognize issues requiring leadership or IRB review.
- Operational judgment: Strong organization, attention to detail, prioritization, and problem-solving skills; ability to manage competing demands and escalate risks appropriately.
- Digital and data systems: Proficiency with Microsoft Office, spreadsheets, participant tracking databases, and digital engagement tools; ability to oversee accurate records and basic campaign reporting.
- Cross-team coordination: Ability to align recruitment and retention activities with scheduling, interview, biomedical, and data operations while maintaining clear accountability.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

- Master’s degree in public health, social or behavioral sciences, health communication, research administration, or a related field.

- Experience managing recruitment and retention for a longitudinal cohort, clinical research study, or similarly complex participant-based program.

- Experience directly supervising research or outreach staff, including coordinators, and conducting performance reviews, coaching, and staff development.

- Experience working with LGBTQ adolescents and young adults, racially and ethnically diverse communities, and/or people living with or affected by HIV in research, public health, or community settings.

- Experience developing community partnerships and outreach initiatives in Chicago.

- Experience overseeing paid digital advertising, social media campaigns, or multimedia outreach with documented evaluation of participant enrollment or engagement outcomes.

- Experience using REDCap or comparable research databases and developing recruitment or retention dashboards and reports.

- Experience managing outreach budgets, vendors, and campaign expenditures in an academic, nonprofit, or public health setting.

- Experience with IRB submissions or amendments related to recruitment materials and participant communications; familiarity with Northwestern research and administrative systems.


**Preferred Competencies: (Skills, knowledge, and abilities)**

- Strategic planning and improvement: Ability to integrate community outreach, paid advertising, referrals, and retention initiatives into a coordinated plan and adapt approaches based on evidence.
- Advanced performance analysis: Ability to evaluate enrollment funnels, cohort representation, attrition patterns, and recruitment cost-effectiveness and communicate findings through clear dashboards and recommendations.
- Chicago community knowledge: Understanding of local LGBTQ, youth, HIV, substance use, and public health service networks and opportunities for effective partnerships.
- Affirming and trauma-informed practice: Ability to guide staff in participant-centered engagement that responds to stigma, mistrust, structural barriers, and differing participant needs.
- Creative communication: Ability to assess and refine visual and written outreach materials for clarity, accessibility, relevance, and audience appeal; familiarity with Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or comparable tools.
- Leadership and change management: Ability to mentor coordinators, build shared accountability, navigate difficult conversations, and implement workflow improvements across teams.
- Digital campaign evaluation: Knowledge of audience targeting, campaign testing, platform analytics, and privacy considerations for research advertising.
- Participant experience improvement: Ability to use participant feedback and Community Advisory Board input to strengthen engagement and reduce barriers to continued participation

_**Benefits:**_

_At Northwestern, we are proud to provide meaningful and competitive benefits. The available benefits package for this position will include health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance; paid vacation and holidays; paid medical/sick and parentalleave;tuition benefits for the employee and dependents; pre-tax and flex spending accounts for commuting and dependent care; generous retirement savings options; and wellness programs. For a comprehensive overview of available benefits, including eligibility details, visit us at https://www.northwestern.edu/hr/benefits/index.html to learn more._

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
At Sword, we’re building AI to heal billions and unlock humanity’s full potential. In doing so, we’re pioneering AI Care, a fundamentally new approach to healthcare built for medical reasoning, safety, and real-time treatment, not generic technology applied after the fact. As both a clinical-centric frontier AI lab and an applied AI platform, Sword is reimagining how care is delivered at scale, removing traditional barriers like appointments, waiting rooms, and stigma so more people can access the care they need—and ultimately get back to lives lived in full.

Since 2020, Sword has expanded across physical therapy, women’s health, cardiometabolic, and mental health, and is now moving beyond the session to a fully AI-native, 24/7 care program that brings physical activity, therapeutic exercise, psychotherapy, nutrition, and behavior change into one connected experience. More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs. Backed by 42 clinical studies, 44+ patents, and more than $500 million raised from leading investors including Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, and Founders Fund, Sword is defining a new standard for healthcare.

AIProficiency at Sword

AI fluency is a core expectation at Sword. Every candidate is assessed against our three-level framework — be ready to share real examples of how AI is already part of how you work.

  • Explorer (Level 1) — Uses AI daily to boost personal productivity

  • Builder (Level 2) — Creates workflows and tools that elevate the whole team

  • Integrator (Level 3) — Embeds AI into products and processes at scale

Every hire must demonstrate at least Level 1. The expected level will vary depending on the seniority of the role.

Role

At Sword, data powers our mission to build a pain‑free world. The Data Platform Team is building the foundation that makes data usable across clinical, operations, AI, and product teams: a modern streaming lakehouse, distributed processing for low‑latency data movement, durable workflows coordinating complex operations, and an API‑first surface that lets producers and consumers serve themselves — without tickets, without infra context, and increasingly through agentic interfaces.

This role is for an engineer who thinks about data platforms as products. You’ve built or operated data systems at scale, you reason fluently from storage format up to query engine, and you want to shape the self‑service and agentic experiences layered on top of that foundation.

To get to know more about our Tech Stack, check here.

What you’ll be doing

  • Design and evolve Sword’s streaming lakehouse - the foundation that every data consumer in the company depends on.

  • Build and operate distributed streaming pipelines that move data at low latency and high reliability.

  • Own the durable workflows that coordinate complex data movement across systems.

  • Shape the platform’s API surface - the interface producers and consumers use so they never need to touch infrastructure.

  • Drive evaluations and integrations with vendor data platforms, sitting inside the architectural trade‑offs rather than just consuming the output.

  • Contribute to the self‑service and agentic layer: interfaces designed to be consumed by humans, systems, and AI agents alike.

  • Partner with data engineers and analysts on contracts, governance, and lineage.

  • Build and maintain AI‑ready data infrastructure that powers ML and AI‑driven products across Sword.

  • Leverage AI coding assistants and LLMs to accelerate development, automate documentation, and raise code quality.

  • Work in a regulated environment where audit, compliance, and governance are part of every design.

What you need to have

  • Proven experience designing and operating data platforms at scale - warehouse, data lake, or lakehouse architectures in production.

  • Hands‑on experience with a modern lakehouse table format - Iceberg strongly preferred; Delta Lake or Hudi also welcome. You understand how the format works under the hood: metadata layout, snapshots, manifests, compaction, copy‑on‑write vs. merge‑on‑read.

  • Clear mental model of catalogs (REST, Polaris, Glue, Unity, Hive) - their trade‑offs, and how compute stays detached from storage.

  • Exposure to at least one vendor lakehouse or query platform - Snowflake, Starburst, or Databricks — at the level where you can reason about its architecture, not just use its UI.

  • Strong experience with a distributed processing engine - Flink strongly preferred; Spark also fine. You can reason about its internals, fine‑tune a running job, and debug a pipeline that’s silently degrading.

  • Familiarity with durable execution - Temporal, Restate, or similar - or at minimum a solid mental model of what durable execution means and why it matters for data workflows.

  • Production experience building and operating APIs (REST or gRPC) at scale - good instincts about contracts, versioning, retries, rate limiting, and observability.

  • Solid understanding of Kafka and event‑driven architectures (producers/consumers, partitioning, delivery semantics).

  • Comfortable in regulated environments (healthcare, fintech, gov) where audit, compliance, and data governance are part of every design.

  • Platform mindset: you design for self‑service, API‑first, and with systems and agents - not only humans - as legitimate consumers.

Bonus

  • Deeper familiarity with open/REST catalogs (Polaris, Nessie, Unity) beyond basic use.

  • Observability stack fluency (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry).

  • Prior work on agentic or AI‑facing API surfaces, or MCP‑style interfaces.

  • Experience in HIPAA, FedRAMP, or SOC 2 environments.

  • dbt, DataHub, or data contract tooling exposure.

Mindset and Collaboration

  • Service orientation: you build APIs (and increasingly agent‑facing tools) that others love to use.

  • Reliability‑first: failure modes, retries, and observability are part of day‑one design.

  • Cross‑functional: you enjoy working with data engineers, analysts, and ML engineers and understanding their problems.

  • Documentation mindset: good APIs come with great docs — and good docs now means machine‑readable too.

  • Iterative: you ship incrementally and improve based on feedback.

*The range below reflects base, variable, and equity for this role.

This is a starting point, not a ceiling — once someone joins and proves they’re outlier talent, we adjust quickly to make sure their compensation matches their impact.

Job titles may span more than one career level, so actual pay depends on skills, qualifications, experience, location, and market demand, among other factors. The range reflects base salary plus any variable, bonus, or sales incentives, and our estimate of the value of private company stock options where applicable. It's subject to change, and future stock value isn't guaranteed. Sword also offers additional benefits beyond total compensation.

Total Compensation Range

€52.500 — €82.500 EUR

Country-specific benefits may vary and will be detailed separately.

title: Microdevices Engineer III
description:
## **Job Details**

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

**Responsibilities:**

The **Communications and Instruments Division** provides leadership in the development and infusion of technologies that enable advanced flight sensors, instruments, and deep space communications. Our expertise spans the entire electromagnetic spectrum—from RF through ultraviolet (UV)—and includes micro-electro-mechanical systems and quantum engineering. We create novel material systems and fabrication techniques that unlock new concepts and mission architectures. We pioneer deep space communication theory, implement advanced communication systems (Earth, planetary surfaces and deep space flight) and develop navigational tracking to understand where we are and how to ensure robust engineering and science data return.

The **Instrument Systems, Microdevices and Sensors Section** develops new technologies spanning quantum, micro- and nano-devices that enable advanced flight sensors and instruments and transitions them to flight infusion. We lead and support Payload and Instrument System Engineering and Instrument Integration and Test functions across D36 product lines, and we partner with academic institutions and science communities. The Central Processing & MDL Support Group maintains and improves the Microdevices Laboratory (MDL) institutional facility on site — its equipment, operations, facilities and safety infrastructure. MDL is dedicated to the study of micro- and nano-fabrication techniques.

We are seeking an experienced **Microdevices Engineer III** with expertise in semiconductor processing equipment maintenance to join our outstanding Microdevices Laboratory team. You will own tools independently, carry authority to release them to service, lead installation and commissioning efforts, and mentor junior staff.  You will be a key member of the Central Processing & MDL Support Group, reporting to the Group Supervisor and working as part of the equipment engineering team led by MDL’s senior lead equipment engineer.

MDL operates a broad installed base of research-grade process tools — spanning lithography, dry etch, physical and chemical vapor deposition, thermal processing, metrology, dicing and packaging. Many are one-of-a-kind, heavily modified, or no longer supported by their original vendor, and our research users depend on their availability. In this role, you will hold ownership of a named set of these tools, keep them qualified and available, and drive durable fixes to the failures that take them down.

**Tasks include, but are not limited to:**

- Hold independent technical ownership of assigned tools, including authority to declare a tool up, conditionally up, or down and to determine what qualification evidence is sufficient for release. Define and run the qualification or test exposure needed to return tools to qualified service for research users. Provide oversight and operation of semiconductor device processing equipment within the facility, including user training, tool sign-off and access qualification.

- Maintain, troubleshoot and repair assigned semiconductor process equipment, including preventive maintenance, source and consumable replacement, chamber and quartz cleaning, pump and cold-trap service, and cryopump regeneration. Diagnose faults across vacuum, RF and plasma, gas delivery and flow control, fieldbus and PLC controls, precision mechanics, optics and legacy tool control computers, including complex cross-disciplinary faults with no documented procedure or incomplete vendor documentation.

- Define and improve preventive maintenance programs, procedures and acceptance criteria, bringing assigned tools under documented, repeatable maintenance. Own the obsolescence and spares strategy for assigned tools.

- Drive root-cause analysis and permanent corrective action on recurring failures, moving the group from repeated part replacement to durable engineering fixes. Contribute to equipment reliability and availability reporting, identifying the dominant contributors to downtime to inform maintenance and investment priorities.

- Maintain the laboratory management system (NEMO) as the system of record: open tickets promptly, record progress, and close with a substantive resolution note describing root cause and corrective action. Issue clear, timely status notifications to the user community when tools go down, return to service or enter scheduled maintenance.

- Lead installation, relocation, commissioning, qualification and startup of new capability end to end, including requirements definition, vendor evaluation, and sole-source and procurement documentation for new equipment acquisitions. Coordinate vendors, facilities, safety and research users. Perform electrical integration, high-voltage and PCB troubleshooting, and electrical and mechanical system testing.

- Manage vendor technical relationships: define and evaluate service contract scope, review quotes and renewals, drive warranty and RMA actions, and direct field service engineers on site. Order, source, expedite and stock equipment spares, chemicals and consumables; manage long-lead and end-of-life parts and make repair-versus-replace recommendations.

- Provide direct processing service for others in conjunction with MDL operations. Mentor and develop junior engineers and technicians, qualify others on tools, and review their maintenance and repair work.

- Serve as backup to the senior lead equipment engineer, including group coordination and user communication. Brief management on equipment status, risk and investment needs.

- Hands-on technical role with significant field work in an operating cleanroom, including heavy lifting of up to 35 pounds.

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Engineering in electrical, electronics, mechanical or a related discipline with a minimum of 6 years of related work experience; or a Master’s degree  in a related discipline with a minimum of 4 years of related work experience; or a PhD degree in a related discipline with a minimum of 2 years of related work experience.

- Demonstrated hands-on experience in the maintenance, upgrade, installation and operation of high-technology semiconductor equipment — lithography (patterning), deposition, wet and dry etching, characterization, dicing, and packaging.

- Knowledge of vacuum technology, including sealing, roughing, high-vacuum and cryogenic pumping systems, and leak detection.

- Knowledge of plasma physics and plasma processing, semiconductor processing, optics, computer control systems, and electronic diagnostics.

- Broad knowledge of the operation and system specifics of lithography steppers and scanners.

- Demonstrated ability to diagnose and repair mechanical systems hands-on.

- Ability to read, interpret and work from schematics, drawings and vendor service documentation.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and computerized maintenance or laboratory management systems.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills and demonstrated ability to work on a team and build work relationships.

- Ability to respond to after-hours emergency calls.

- Ability and willingness to use a respirator.

- Demonstrated ability to independently own process tools and make release-to-service decisions affecting downstream research results; demonstrated experience in root-cause analysis of recurring equipment failures; and demonstrated experience leading vendor service relationships.

**Preferred Skills:**

- Wide-ranging knowledge in at least one semiconductor processing area involving innovative processing equipment.

- Ability to detect and repair electronics at the component level.

- Experience with fieldbus and PLC-based tool controls, distributed I/O diagnostics, and interlock and safety logic.

- Experience with mass flow controllers, RF power generation and delivery, and high-purity gas delivery and piping systems.

- Experience with process chillers, heat exchangers and process cooling water systems.

- Experience sustaining legacy and vendor-unsupported tool platforms, including control computer replacement and recovery, and addressing IT cybersecurity requirements for networked tools.

- Proficiency in diagnosing and remedying computer problems and in building and configuring networked tool connections within cybersecurity requirements.

- Experience leading installation and commissioning of advanced lithography tools, such as deep-UV steppers or step-and-scan systems.

- Experience with equipment reliability methods, availability metrics, and data-driven maintenance prioritization.

- Experience mentoring junior engineers and technicians and developing training and qualification programs.

- Knowledge of life safety system monitoring and controls, cleanroom technology and operations, contamination control, electrostatic discharge control, and facilities construction and maintenance interfaces (structural, electrical, plumbing — UHP water and UHP gas, HVAC).

- Knowledge of Si, GaAs, GaN and superconductor processing, and general chemistry.

- Experience in a shared-user research, university nanofabrication, industrial or government laboratory environment.

- Excellent interpersonal skills, with proficiency in communicating across a wide range of technical backgrounds and educational levels — scientific staff and facility trades as well as outside regulatory agencies and inspectors.

- Strong ability to multi-task and prioritize competing tool-down situations.

title: Cloud Security Engineer
location: San Antonio, Heredia Province, Costa Rica
description:
Position Summary


The Cloud Security Engineer will design, implement, and maintain scalable security controls and automated guardrails across enterprise cloud environments, including AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

This role will focus on strengthening cloud security through secure-by-default architectures, Infrastructure as Code, Policy as Code, security automation, cloud security posture management, and continuous control improvement. The engineer will collaborate with Cloud Platform Engineering, DevOps, Security Architecture, Cloud Center of Excellence, Security Operations, Infrastructure, and application teams to integrate security throughout cloud infrastructure and application deployment lifecycles.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate strong hands-on cloud security engineering expertise and the ability to develop and operationalize security solutions that reduce risk, improve compliance, and enable secure cloud adoption at enterprise scale.


What will you do:


  • Design, implement, and maintain cloud security controls, secure configuration standards, and automated guardrails across AWS, Azure, and/or GCP environments.
  • Develop and enforce security guardrails through Policy as Code using native cloud policy engines and technologies such as Azure Policy, AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs), Terraform policy checks, and Open Policy Agent (OPA).
  • Integrate automated security validation, compliance checks, and security controls into Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Engineer and maintain cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls, enforcing least privilege, secure workload identities, and Zero Trust principles.
  • Design and implement defense-in-depth network security controls, including segmentation, secure ingress/egress, private connectivity, firewalls, and Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) across cloud and hybrid environments.
  • Implement security controls for containers, Kubernetes, serverless workloads, and cloud-native architectures, including workload identity, network security, image scanning, and secure configurations.
  • Collaborate with DevOps and Platform Engineering teams to develop reusable secure-by-default deployment patterns and automate remediation of cloud security misconfigurations.
  • Implement, maintain, and operationalize cloud security monitoring and posture management capabilities using CSPM/CNAPP and native cloud security services.
  • Implement and validate cloud security logging, monitoring, encryption, key management, and secrets management controls.
  • Conduct cloud architecture and security control assessments to identify risks, configuration weaknesses, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Support compliance with corporate security policies and applicable regulatory requirements through technical security controls and maintain supporting security standards, procedures, and documentation.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to troubleshoot cloud security issues, address security findings, and improve the effectiveness of cloud security controls.

What you need:


  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
  • Relevant cloud security certifications, such as AWS Certified Security – Specialty, Microsoft Azure Security Engineer Associate, or Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer, are preferred.
  • Advanced security certifications, such as CCSP, CISSP, or CISM, are considered an advantage.
  • Equivalent demonstrated hands-on cloud security engineering experience will be considered

Qualifications & Experience



  • 5+ years of hands-on cloud security experience, with strong technical expertise in at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
  • Hands-on experience implementing cloud security controls, including IAM, workload identities, least-privilege access, network security, encryption, key management, secrets management, logging, and security monitoring.
  • Experience implementing security controls for containers, Kubernetes, serverless, and cloud-native architecture
  • Hands-on experience developing or implementing Policy as Code using Azure Policy, AWS SCPs, OPA, or equivalent technologies.
  • Experience integrating security controls and automated validation into Infrastructure as Code and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language, such as Python, PowerShell, or Bash, for security automation.
  • Experience implementing and operationalizing CSPM, CNAPP, CWPP, or equivalent cloud security capabilities.
  • Strong understanding of cloud security architecture, defense-in-depth, Zero Trust, and least-privilege principles.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with Cloud Platform Engineering, DevOps, Infrastructure, IAM, Application Engineering, and Security Operations teams.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience securing multi-cloud or hybrid-cloud environments.
  • Advanced experience securing Kubernetes, container orchestration platforms, and serverless architectures.
  • Experience integrating cloud security telemetry into enterprise SIEM platforms and security operations workflows.
  • Experience designing or implementing security controls for cloud-based AI/ML services.
  • Familiarity with security frameworks and standards, including NIST, CIS Benchmarks, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and PCI DSS.

description:

Backed by over $100M from top investors including Google Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, Andreessen Horowitz, and Coatue, we’re a team that challenges the status quo and moves fast at the intersection of AI and healthcare. title: Energy Development Manager in , United States
description:
Description
Position Summary
Piedmont Service Group is seeking a customer-facing, results-oriented Energy Development Manager to help grow our Energy & Sustainability Services (ESS) business while supporting sales teams across the organization in NC/SC/VA. Reporting to the Vice President / Director of Sales, this position serves as a strategic resource to project sales representatives, maintenance sales representatives, General Managers, operations leaders, and customers in identifying, developing, and helping close energy-driven HVAC, controls, infrastructure, and capital improvement projects.
This is not a traditional back-office engineering role. The Energy Development Manager will combine technical credibility, business development ability, financial analysis, and project-development leadership. The role will help develop hybrid energy savings projects, expand HVAC controls and BAS modernization opportunities, support major capital replacement initiatives, and lead the continued development of ESS tools, resources, and team capabilities.
Why Join PSG
This is an opportunity to help shape the future of Energy & Sustainability Services within one of the region's leading commercial HVAC organizations. The Energy Development Manager will play a key role in supporting customer success, driving project growth, expanding energy and controls solutions, and building the next of ESS capability across the company.
Key Responsibilities
Energy Project Development & Sales Support
* Work closely with Project Sales Representatives, Maintenance Sales Representatives, General Managers, and other sales team members to identify, develop, and support hybrid energy savings projects involving HVAC upgrades, controls modernization, infrastructure improvements, utility incentives, operational savings, and lifecycle cost reduction.
* Conduct customer discovery meetings, site assessments, facility evaluations, and strategic planning discussions and help convert customer facility challenges into funded projects.
* Serve as a technical and financial resource during customer presentations, sales strategy sessions, and executive-level project discussions.
Capital Planning & Major Project Support
* Serve as a primary ESS resource for large capital replacement and infrastructure improvement opportunities using lifecycle cost analysis, technical review, energy savings estimates, and utility incentive review.
* Help sales teams identify, prioritize, and communicate long-term facility capital needs.
* Develop practical business cases that connect equipment replacement, building performance, reduced operating cost, risk reduction, and improved customer decision-making.
* Create, maintain, and improve ESS tools, templates, and models that make project development more consistent and repeatable.
HVAC Controls & Building Automation Growth
* Make HVAC controls and BAS modernization a specific focus of ESS growth by partnering with controls, service, operations, and project sales teams to identify BAS upgrades, controls optimization.
* Incorporate controls strategies into energy audits, CAPEX planning, hybrid energy savings projects, and customer ROI discussions.
* Help customers understand the energy, operational, comfort, reliability, and financial benefits of modernized controls and optimized building automation systems.
Customer & Sales Team Engagement
* Serve as a trusted advisor to customers, sales representatives, General Managers, operations leaders, and company leadership by participating in customer meetings, facility assessments, proposal reviews, project strategy discussions, and executive-level presentations.
* Support a collaborative team-selling environment across sales, operations, controls, service, and construction teams and assist sales teams in developing strategies for large, complex, and financially driven opportunities.
* Act as the primary liaison between ESS, project sales teams, maintenance sales teams, General Managers, and executive leadership to ensure ESS resources remain aligned with company growth objectives.
Energy Analysis & Business Case Development
* Lead or oversee facility assessments, energy evaluations, savings analyses, utility reviews, incentive research, and financial modeling. Review calculations, assumptions, and reports developed by ESS staff, vendors, interns, or supporting partners.
* Ensure recommendations are technically sound, financially practical, and aligned with customer objectives.
* Translate complex technical information into practical business recommendations for customers and internal teams.
Performance Contract & M&V Support
* Maintain oversight of existing Measurement & Verification (M&V) obligations and long-term energy performance commitments.
* Assist with future performance-contract opportunities when appropriate while recognizing that hybrid energy savings projects are expected to be the larger growth model.
ESS Leadership & Team Development
* Lead and develop the Energy & Sustainability Services Team as a scalable sales-support and project-development resource by managing and mentoring energy engineers, interns, analysts, etc.
* Establish consistent processes, reporting standards, calculation methodologies, proposal support tools, and project-development templates.
* Promote collaboration between ESS, sales teams, operations, controls, and executive leadership.
Requirements
Required Qualifications
* 10+ years of experience in commercial HVAC, mechanical contracting, project development, energy services, controls, facility infrastructure, technical sales support, or related industries.
* Strong customer-facing communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
* Experience supporting project development, capital planning, engineering consulting, technical sales support, energy services, and financial justifications for capital improvement projects.
* Working knowledge of commercial HVAC systems, controls, facility operations, energy savings principles.
* Ability to translate technical information into practical business value for customers and internal teams.
* Strong Excel, financial modeling, report writing, and presentation skills.
* Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team-selling environment.
* Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple opportunities, priorities, and stakeholders.
* Ability to travel overnight up to 25%
Qualifications
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, energy management, business, or related technical discipline.
* Professional Engineer (PE) license, Certified Energy Manager (CEM) certification or MBA
* Experience with performance contracting, Measurement & Verification, utility incentives, energy services agreements, HVAC controls, BAS modernization, and controls optimization,
